d: Australian courts have convicted Border Force and state police officers of assisting importations through Sydney and Melbourne, in cases brought after the law enforcement integrity commission's referrals. Australia pays the highest wholesale prices of any market on this map, which is what the insider is being paid against.
cite: Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity annual reports and referrals; NSW and Victorian court judgments, 2016-2024

n: Border services officers
d: Canada Border Services Agency officers have been convicted of waving vehicles through at the Windsor-Detroit and Pacific Highway crossings. The agency had no independent civilian oversight body until legislation was brought forward in the 2020s, which is unusual among comparable agencies.
cite: Ontario and British Columbia court judgments, 2014-2023; CBSA internal affairs reporting; Public Safety Canada oversight legislation

n: Senior police and the protection economy
d: The deputy national police chief was removed and investigated in 2023 over an alleged protection relationship with an online gambling network, in a case that split the police leadership publicly. The charges concern gambling proceeds rather than narcotics, but the protection mechanism and the laundering rails are the same ones the trade uses.
cite: Royal Thai Police disciplinary proceedings and Thai Office of the Attorney-General filings, 2023-2024

n: Officers at the western crossings
d: Ukrainian anti-corruption bodies have charged customs and border service officers at the Zakarpattia crossings with running contraband channels into the European Union. The charges concern smuggling generally rather than narcotics specifically; the crossings are the same ones used by the eastern corridor on this map's route layer.
cite: Ukrainian National Anti-Corruption Bureau and State Bureau of Investigation case records, 2022-2024

n: Jimmy Cherizier — former police officer, sanctioned gang leader
d: A serving officer of the Haitian National Police until 2018, subsequently the leader of the largest federation of armed groups in Port-au-Prince and the first individual designated under the UN's Haiti sanctions regime in 2022. The trajectory from the force to the federation, rather than any single act, is what this entry records.
cite: UN Security Council Resolution 2653 designation, October 2022; US and Canadian sanctions designations; UN Panel of Experts on Haiti reports

n: TD Bank
d: The first bank in US history to plead guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. It admitted three networks moved more than $670 million through its accounts over six years against $18.3 trillion in unmonitored activity. Employees including a store manager were bribed; one took $11,000 in retail gift cards. Penalties totalled about $3.09 billion, with an asset cap on its US units.
cite: US v. TD Bank NA, D.N.J., guilty plea October 2024
rank: Retail bank — branch staff and compliance (banks & money transmission)

n: Credit Suisse
d: Convicted by the Swiss Federal Criminal Court of failing to prevent money laundering by a Bulgarian cocaine-trafficking organisation, alongside a former relationship manager. The first criminal conviction of a major Swiss bank in the country's history.
cite: Bundesstrafgericht / Tribunal pénal fédéral, Bellinzona, June 2022
rank: Private bank — relationship management (banks & money transmission)

n: HSBC
d: Deferred prosecution and $1.9 billion after US authorities found its Mexican affiliate had moved Sinaloa and Norte del Valle proceeds through bulk cash deposits its monitoring did not catch. No individual executive was prosecuted; the DPA expired without charges.
cite: US v. HSBC Bank USA NA, E.D.N.Y., DPA December 2012
rank: Global bank — Mexican affiliate (banks & money transmission)
who: Sinaloa and Norte del Valle cartels

n: Wachovia
d: Between 2004 and 2007 the bank took some $378 billion from thirteen Mexican currency exchange houses through correspondent accounts, money used among other things to buy aircraft for trafficking. In March 2010 it entered a deferred prosecution agreement in the Southern District of Florida: $110 million forfeited and a $50 million fine, at the time the largest penalty ever imposed for a Bank Secrecy Act violation. Charges were dismissed a year later on compliance with the agreement. No executive was prosecuted, and the sum is a fraction of one year's profit at the bank.
cite: US v. Wachovia Bank N.A., S.D. Fla., deferred prosecution agreement approved 17 March 2010, Case No. 10-20165-CR-LENARD; consent agreements with the OCC and FinCEN; Wells Fargo Form 8-K, 17 March 2010
rank: Global bank — correspondent banking (banks & money transmission)

n: Rabobank National Association
d: The California subsidiary of the Dutch bank pleaded guilty in February 2018 to a felony conspiracy charge and paid $368.7 million, the largest financial penalty in the Southern District of California. The offence is not the laundering itself: the bank admitted conspiring with former executives to obstruct an examination by its regulator, concealing the deficiencies in its anti-money-laundering programme after learning that large numbers of customer transactions indicated trafficking and organised crime. A former vice-president had taken a deferred prosecution agreement two months earlier and was cooperating.
cite: US v. Rabobank National Association, S.D. Cal., guilty plea 7 February 2018 before Magistrate Judge Jill Burkhardt; Department of Justice statement; deferred prosecution agreement with a former vice-president, 14 December 2017

n: Banamex USA (Citigroup)
d: Forfeited $97 million under a non-prosecution agreement over failures in monitoring remittances to Mexico, where a small compliance staff generated fewer than ten suspicious activity reports against millions of transactions flagged by its own systems.
cite: US DOJ non-prosecution agreement, May 2017

n: Danske Bank — Estonia branch
d: Pleaded guilty to bank fraud conspiracy and forfeited $2 billion over roughly €200 billion in non-resident flows through a single branch. Laundering infrastructure rather than drug-specific: the same channel serves any proceeds needing distance from their origin.
cite: US v. Danske Bank A/S, S.D.N.Y., plea December 2022
rank: Correspondent banking — non-resident portfolio (banks & money transmission)

n: Western Union
d: The company entered a deferred prosecution agreement on 19 January 2017 admitting willful failure to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering programme and aiding and abetting wire fraud between 2004 and 2012, and forfeited $586 million — the largest forfeiture ever imposed on a money services business — to be used to reimburse defrauded consumers. The specific failure is the one worth recording: it filed suspicious activity reports about its customers but not about its own agents, whom it knew were complicit. Prosecutors said employees fought to keep high-volume agents because of their turnover. Twenty-six agents in the United States and Canada had already been convicted since 2001. New York fined the company a further $60 million in 2018 and France penalised it in 2019.
cite: US Department of Justice and Federal Trade Commission deferred prosecution agreement and consent order, 19 January 2017, with the US Attorneys for the Middle and Eastern Districts of Pennsylvania, the Central District of California and the Southern District of Florida; FinCEN civil money penalty; New York Department of Financial Services penalty, 2018
rank: Money transmission — agent network (banks & money transmission)

n: Westpac
d: Paid an A$1.3 billion civil penalty, the largest in Australian history, over roughly 23 million reporting breaches. Cited here as scale evidence on monitoring failure rather than as a drug case.
cite: AUSTRAC v. Westpac Banking Corporation, Federal Court of Australia, 2020

n: ING Groep
d: Settled with Dutch prosecutors for €775 million after clients used its accounts for laundering over years while customer due diligence was under-resourced. No individuals were charged, a decision later challenged in the Dutch courts.
cite: Openbaar Ministerie settlement, September 2018
rank: Universal bank — client onboarding (banks & money transmission)

n: ABLV Bank
d: Named by FinCEN as a primary money-laundering concern; the designation triggered a deposit run and the bank's self-liquidation within weeks. A demonstration that designation can end an institution without a trial.
cite: FinCEN Section 311 notice of proposed rulemaking, February 2018
rank: Correspondent bank — shell-company clients (banks & money transmission)

n: Banca Privada d'Andorra
d: FinCEN found in March 2015 that high-level managers had knowingly processed transactions for third-party launderers acting for transnational criminal organisations, moving hundreds of millions through four US correspondent banks. Andorra took over the bank the next day and wound it up within the week, splitting it into a continuing bank and a bad bank; clients had to prove their own funds legitimate to recover them. In July 2025 a court sentenced eighteen executives, the former chief executive to seven years and a 30 million euro fine. The defendants are appealing, and shareholders argue the bank was closed on an administrative finding without evidence tested in court. Some clients named in the case have never been convicted.
cite: FinCEN Section 311 notice of finding, 10 March 2015; Andorran intervention and liquidation, March 2015; Andorran court sentences, July 2025
rank: Private bank — third-party laundering (banks & money transmission)

n: Binance
d: Pleaded guilty to Bank Secrecy Act and sanctions violations and agreed to $4.3 billion in penalties; its founder pleaded guilty personally. Filings describe transactions with darknet markets and ransomware actors passing through with no effective monitoring.
cite: US v. Binance Holdings Ltd, W.D. Wash., plea November 2023

n: BTC-e / Alexander Vinnik
d: An exchange indicted as a laundering vehicle for roughly $4 billion, including narcotics proceeds; its operator was arrested in Greece, convicted in France, and later pleaded guilty in the United States.
cite: US v. BTC-e and Vinnik, N.D. Cal., indictment 2017; US plea 2024

n: Hydra Market
d: Seized by German police with its servers and about €23 million in bitcoin, and sanctioned by the US Treasury the same day. It was the largest darknet drug marketplace, with laundering services sold alongside the product.
cite: BKA seizure and OFAC designation, April 2022

n: Tornado Cash
d: Sanctioned by OFAC as a laundering tool; a developer was convicted in the Netherlands in 2024. The US designation was later vacated in part on appeal, leaving the question of whether software can be sanctioned unresolved.
cite: OFAC designation August 2022; Van der Linde ruling, Rechtbank Oost-Brabant, 2024; Van Loon v. Treasury, 5th Cir., 2024

n: MSC Gayane — 20 tonnes and the crew list
d: Roughly 20 tonnes of cocaine were seized from a Mediterranean Shipping Company vessel in Philadelphia in 2019, the largest such seizure in US history at the time. Eight seafarers pleaded guilty, among them the chief mate and second mate, drawing about 50 years between them; the ship was released after the operator posted security. The cargo was not loaded at an export terminal but taken aboard at night at sea, which puts the vulnerability in the crew list rather than the container manifest. The operator called itself a victim and said it was spending over 00 million on security in response.
cite: US v. Vasquez Reyes, Penda, Ilic, Kavaja and others, E.D. Pa., pleas and sentences 2019-2022
rank: Container vessel — chief mate, second mate and crew (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Port of Antwerp — terminal access and scanning data
d: Antwerp handles the largest cocaine volumes in Europe, and the terminal operators sit at the point of attack: container reference codes, gate access and scanning records are commercial systems, and the people with them are recruited rather than the cargo intercepted. Seizures reached 116 tonnes in 2023 alone. The port authority and operators have since restricted access and rotated codes; the EU review of port corruption found the vulnerability is staff access rather than screening technology.
cite: Antwerp port authority and terminal operator measures, 2022-2024; EUDA and World Customs Organization joint report, 2025
rank: Container terminals — hiring, gate systems and scan records (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Port of Rotterdam — 'uithalers' networks
d: Prosecutions of container extraction crews, including cases where terminal employees supplied PIN codes from the port's own release system. The vulnerability is administrative access rather than physical security.
cite: Rotterdam District Court proceedings, multiple, 2019–2024
rank: Terminal access and IT systems (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Guayaquil banana corridor
d: Ecuador's cocaine exports move inside legitimate fruit shipments; national seizure volumes rose alongside export growth, and prosecutions have reached exporters, port staff and customs officials. Ecuador's criminality score rose to 7.48 in the 2025 Index.
cite: Fiscalia General del Estado prosecutions; UNODC seizure reporting
rank: Export logistics and cold chain (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Amarvel Biotech and other PRC precursor suppliers
d: US indictments charged China-based chemical companies and their executives with trafficking fentanyl precursors, alleging they marketed the chemicals to Mexican buyers and advised on concealing shipments. The companies are outside US jurisdiction in practice.
cite: US v. Amarvel Biotech et al., S.D.N.Y., indictments June 2023

n: Precursor diversion — acetic anhydride
d: The reagent required to convert morphine into heroin is a mainstream industrial chemical. The INCB tracks legitimate trade and repeatedly reports diversion at the distribution layer rather than at manufacture, which is where controls are weakest.
cite: INCB Precursors Report, annual

n: McKesson, Cardinal Health, AmerisourceBergen
d: The three largest US drug distributors agreed to pay about $21 billion over 18 years to settle claims that they shipped opioid volumes their own monitoring systems flagged. Diversion out of a licensed supply chain, not capture by an outside group.
cite: National Prescription Opiate Litigation, N.D. Ohio, settlement July 2021

n: Purdue Pharma
d: Pleaded guilty to three felonies including conspiracy to defraud the United States and violating the anti-kickback statute, with $8.3 billion in penalties. The Sackler settlement structure was rejected by the Supreme Court in 2024 and renegotiated.
cite: US v. Purdue Pharma LP, D.N.J., plea November 2020; Harrington v. Purdue Pharma, 2024

n: Rochester Drug Co-Operative
d: The first US distributor charged criminally over opioid diversion; its former chief executive was later convicted. Establishing personal criminal liability at this layer took two decades of the epidemic.
cite: US v. Rochester Drug Co-Operative, S.D.N.Y., deferred prosecution 2019; US v. Doud, conviction 2022

n: Suncity Group
d: Its chairman was convicted in Macau of running a criminal syndicate and illegal gambling and sentenced to 18 years. Junket credit systems moved value across borders in a form that generated no bank record.
cite: Court of First Instance, Macau SAR, January 2023

n: Crown Resorts
d: A NSW commission found the company unsuitable to hold a licence after evidence that junket partners with organised-crime links used its accounts to move funds; AUSTRAC later obtained a A$450 million penalty.
cite: Bergin Inquiry report, February 2021; AUSTRAC v. Crown, Federal Court, 2023

n: Wynn Las Vegas
d: Forfeited $130 million to resolve allegations it let unlicensed money transmitting move funds for foreign patrons. The mechanism was informal value transfer routed around the banking system entirely.
cite: US DOJ non-prosecution agreement, September 2024

n: Mossack Fonseca
d: The firm at the centre of the Panama Papers; its founders and 26 others were acquitted of money laundering by a Panamanian court in 2024, the judge citing insufficient and improperly gathered evidence. The acquittal is the record and belongs on the map as much as a conviction would.
cite: Duodécimo Juzgado Penal, Panama, verdict June 2024
rank: Offshore formation agent (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: UK company formation — Scottish Limited Partnerships
d: Structures registered in the UK for a few pounds, with no verified beneficial owner until recent reform, appeared repeatedly in laundering schemes traced by journalists and regulators. Not a firm but a jurisdictional product, and the reason gatekeeper prosecutions are so rare.
cite: UK Government SLP consultation and reform; Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023
rank: Corporate registry as a service (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Phantom Secure
d: Its chief executive pleaded guilty to running a criminal enterprise, the first US prosecution of a company for knowingly supplying encrypted devices to trafficking organisations. Devices were sold with the camera and microphone removed.
cite: US v. Ramos, S.D. Cal., plea October 2018
rank: Encrypted handset provider — chief executive (encrypted communications)

n: Sky Global / Sky ECC
d: Its chief executive was indicted in the United States for racketeering; Belgian and Dutch police had already penetrated the network, producing about a billion messages that underpinned hundreds of European prosecutions. Five years on the charges remain untried: the company’s distributor spent four years in a French jail before release on bail in 2025 and awaits a trial listed for late 2026, and both men maintain their innocence. The evidence the takedown produced has convicted hundreds of others in the meantime.
cite: US v. Eap, S.D. Cal., indictment March 2021; Belgian federal police operation, March 2021; French proceedings against the distributor, bail June 2025, trial listed late 2026

n: EncroChat
d: French and Dutch authorities compromised the network's servers in 2020. The resulting material produced thousands of arrests across Europe and remains the single largest evidentiary source in modern European organised-crime prosecutions; its admissibility has been litigated in several countries.
cite: Operation Emma/Lemont, Eurojust, 2020; national admissibility rulings 2021–2024

n: NTR Metals / Elemetal
d: Three traders were convicted or pleaded guilty over a scheme importing roughly $3.6 billion in illegally mined South American gold, laundering drug proceeds through metal purchases. Gold converts cash into an exportable commodity with a legitimate invoice.
cite: US v. Barrage, Granda and Rodriguez, S.D. Fla., pleas 2017–2018
rank: Gold refiner — trading desk (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Chiquita Brands International
d: Pleaded guilty in US federal court to making payments to the AUC, a designated terrorist organisation and one of Colombia's largest cocaine traffickers, and paid a $25 million fine. A Florida jury found the company liable in a civil case brought by victims' families in 2024.
cite: US v. Chiquita Brands International, D.D.C., plea March 2007; civil verdict S.D. Fla., June 2024

n: Dubai gold trade — Kaloti and the refining chain
d: A DEA-led task force spent three years assembling a case against one of the world’s largest gold traders and refiners, concluding it bought metal from sellers suspected of laundering for drug traffickers, often paying cash and wiring funds for suspect clients. Treasury abandoned the case. An auditor’s 2012 inspection had already found .2 billion in cash-for-gold deals, about 45 percent of the firm’s business that year, and 2.4 tonnes taken in more than a thousand transactions from customers who provided no paperwork; the partner who reported it was forced out and sued his firm. Dubai’s regulator removed the refinery from its approved list in 2015. The company denies the allegations and continues to trade.
cite: Ernst & Young inspection report, 2012, and whistleblower disclosure, 2014; DMCC delisting, 2015; ICIJ FinCEN Files reporting on the abandoned Treasury case, 2020-2024
rank: Gold refining and bullion trading — cash purchase (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Lebanese Canadian Bank
d: Named by FinCEN as a primary money-laundering concern for moving proceeds of a cocaine network that shipped through West Africa and settled its accounts by buying used cars in the United States for resale in Africa. The bank's assets were sold and its successor forfeited $102 million; no banker was prosecuted.
cite: FinCEN Section 311 finding, February 2011; US v. Lebanese Canadian Bank SAL, S.D.N.Y., settlement August 2013
rank: Retail and correspondent bank — used-car trade finance (banks & money transmission)

n: Banco Continental (Honduras)
d: Designated by OFAC alongside its owners, a former vice-president's family, as a laundering vehicle for the Cachiros trafficking organisation. Honduran regulators put it into liquidation within days of the designation, and depositors were paid out over the following year.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, October 2015; CNBS liquidation order, October 2015
rank: Domestic bank — owner-controlled lending (banks & money transmission)

n: Banco Delta Asia
d: Designated by FinCEN over accounts held for North Korean entities, including proceeds described as coming from narcotics and counterfeit currency. The action froze roughly $25 million and cut the bank out of dollar clearing; it is the clearest demonstration that a designation reaches further than a prosecution.
cite: FinCEN Section 311 finding, September 2005; final rule 2007
rank: Small bank — sovereign client accounts (banks & money transmission), Macau

n: FBME Bank
d: Registered in Tanzania and operated from Cyprus, it was named by FinCEN as a primary money-laundering concern over accounts used by organised crime and sanctioned parties. Cyprus resolved the bank; the owners' arbitration against the designation ran for years afterwards.
cite: FinCEN Section 311 notice, July 2014; final rule 2016
rank: Offshore bank — non-resident shell accounts (banks & money transmission)

n: U.S. Bancorp
d: Deferred prosecution and $613 million in penalties after admitting it capped the number of alerts its monitoring software could generate so that the workload matched the size of its compliance staff. The bank also failed to report a customer running an unlicensed payday lending business.
cite: US v. U.S. Bank National Association, S.D.N.Y., DPA February 2018
rank: Retail bank — transaction monitoring (banks & money transmission)

n: Capital One
d: Fined $390 million by FinCEN over its Check Cashing Group unit, which processed roughly $16 billion for clients including businesses whose organised-crime associations the bank's own files had recorded. The relationships continued for years after the warnings.
cite: FinCEN consent order, January 2021
rank: Correspondent banking — check-cashing clients (banks & money transmission)

n: MoneyGram International
d: A 2012 deferred prosecution and $100 million forfeiture over agents processing fraud and structured transfers was followed in 2018 by a further $125 million when the company was found to have breached the agreement's terms. The agent model puts the compliance duty on thousands of small franchises and the penalty on the brand.
cite: US v. MoneyGram International Inc., M.D. Pa., DPA November 2012; amended settlement November 2018
rank: Money transmission — agent network (banks & money transmission)

n: Deutsche Bank
d: Fined about $630 million by US and UK regulators over mirror trades that moved roughly $10 billion out of Russia through its Moscow, London and New York desks, and a further $150 million by New York in 2020 for onboarding failures. Laundering infrastructure rather than a drug case: the same channel carries any proceeds that need distance from their origin.
cite: NYDFS and FCA consent orders, January 2017; NYDFS consent order, July 2020
rank: Correspondent banking — mirror trades (banks & money transmission)

n: Swedbank
d: Fined 4 billion kronor by the Swedish regulator over high-risk non-resident flows through its Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian branches and misleading disclosures about them. The Baltic corridor's laundering capacity outlived the Danske case by several years.
cite: Finansinspektionen decision, March 2020
rank: Baltic branch network — non-resident flows (banks & money transmission)

n: ABN AMRO
d: Settled with Dutch prosecutors for €480 million after admitting years of failures in customer checks and reporting. Three former executives were separately named as suspects, which is rare: in most cases at this scale the institution pays and no individual is charged.
cite: Openbaar Ministerie settlement, April 2021
rank: Universal bank — client due diligence (banks & money transmission)

n: Silk Road
d: The first large anonymous drug marketplace, handling several hundred million dollars in sales before its seizure in 2013. Its operator was convicted on seven counts and sentenced to life without parole in 2015; he was pardoned in January 2025 and released.
cite: US v. Ulbricht, S.D.N.Y., verdict February 2015, sentence May 2015; presidential pardon January 2025
undone: Operator pardoned by the US president in January 2025 and released from a life sentence.

n: AlphaBay
d: Ten times the size of Silk Road at its peak and seized in a joint operation in July 2017. Its administrator was arrested in Bangkok and died in custody a week later, which ended the prosecution before any of the evidence was tested.
cite: US Department of Justice and Europol operation, July 2017; S.D. Fla. indictment

n: Hansa Market
d: Dutch police took over the market's servers and ran it themselves for 27 days, collecting addresses and passwords from users fleeing the AlphaBay seizure. The tactic reversed the usual sequence: the takedown came after the surveillance rather than instead of it.
cite: Dutch National Police and Europol, Operation Bayonet, July 2017
rank: Darknet marketplace — covert operation (crypto & digital rails)

n: Wall Street Market
d: Three German administrators were arrested in 2019 after attempting to abscond with roughly €11 million held in escrow. They were convicted in Germany; a US indictment named them and two prolific vendors.
cite: Landgericht Kleve proceedings, verdicts 2021; C.D. Cal. indictment, May 2019

n: Helix
d: A mixing service that laundered roughly 350,000 bitcoin, much of it from darknet drug markets it partnered with directly. Its operator pleaded guilty to a laundering conspiracy and was fined $60 million by FinCEN — the first such penalty against a mixer.
cite: US v. Harmon, D.D.C., plea August 2021; FinCEN civil penalty, October 2020

n: Bitcoin Fog
d: The longest-running mixing service, moving about 1.2 million bitcoin over a decade, a large share of it darknet drug proceeds. Its operator was convicted at trial in March 2024 on blockchain analysis that reached back to transactions made in 2011.
cite: US v. Sterlingov, D.D.C., verdict March 2024, sentence November 2024

n: Bitzlato
d: Named by FinCEN as a primary money-laundering concern in the first use of a new sanctions authority. Officials described over $700 million in transfers with Hydra alone between 2018 and 2022, in both directions: buyers funded purchases from Bitzlato accounts and vendors sent the takings back to them.
cite: FinCEN order under Section 9714(a), January 2023; US v. Legkodymov, E.D.N.Y.
rank: Exchange — deposits from darknet markets (crypto & digital rails)

n: Garantex
d: Sanctioned by OFAC in April 2022 for processing proceeds from Hydra and ransomware operators. Estonia had already withdrawn its licence; the exchange kept operating from Moscow, which is the practical limit of designating an entity inside a jurisdiction that will not act on it.
cite: OFAC designation, April 2022; Estonian FIU licence revocation, February 2022

n: ChipMixer
d: German and US authorities seized the service's servers and about €44 million in bitcoin, citing roughly $700 million in laundered funds from darknet markets and ransomware. It broke deposits into uniform chips so that no output amount could be matched to an input.
cite: BKA and US Department of Justice seizure, March 2023

n: Incognito Market
d: A market that sold prescription pills, many of them counterfeit and fentanyl-laced, and closed by extorting its own users with the threat of publishing their transaction records. Its operator was arrested at JFK in May 2024 and charged in Manhattan.
cite: US v. Rui-Siang Lin, S.D.N.Y., complaint May 2024

n: Port of Hamburg — terminal access
d: Sixteen tonnes of cocaine hidden in tins of putty were found in a single Hamburg container in February 2021, the largest seizure in Europe at the time. German prosecutions have reached dock workers and hauliers; volumes rose here as Antwerp and Rotterdam hardened, which is displacement rather than growth.
cite: German customs (Zoll) seizure announcement, February 2021; Hamburg court proceedings
rank: Container terminals — dock and clearance staff (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Gioia Tauro container port
d: Italy's largest transhipment port sits in the province the 'Ndrangheta holds most completely. Anti-mafia investigations have documented control over hiring and container handling; the seizure figures published each year are the visible fraction of what moves through it.
cite: Direzione Investigativa Antimafia semi-annual reports; Reggio Calabria DDA proceedings
rank: Transhipment terminal — labour and clearance (shipping, freight & ports)

n: The Zheng fentanyl network
d: A father and son were indicted in Ohio and designated by OFAC as a fentanyl trafficking organisation that manufactured analogues to order and shipped them by post to buyers in at least 25 countries. Both remain in China; the case established the pattern the later precursor indictments follow.
cite: US v. Fujing Zheng and Guanghua Zheng, N.D. Ohio, indictment 2018; OFAC designation August 2019
rank: Chemical manufacture and mail-order export (chemicals & precursors)

n: Indian opioid exports to West Africa
d: An investigation traced tapentadol and carisoprodol combinations, unapproved for sale in either the exporting or the importing country, from Indian manufacturers to street markets in Ghana, Nigeria and Cote d'Ivoire. India's drug regulator suspended export permissions and inspected the plants named; the companies deny wrongdoing.
cite: BBC Eye investigation, February 2025; CDSCO enforcement action, 2025

n: Insys Therapeutics
d: The founder and four executives were convicted of racketeering for bribing prescribers to write a fentanyl spray licensed only for cancer breakthrough pain, and running a unit that lied to insurers to get the prescriptions covered. The founder was sentenced to 66 months; the company filed for bankruptcy days after pleading guilty.
cite: US v. Kapoor et al., D. Mass., verdict May 2019, sentence January 2020
rank: Manufacturer — sales force and prior authorisation (pharmaceutical supply)

n: Walmart, CVS and Walgreens
d: The three chains agreed to pay about $13.8 billion over 15 years to settle claims that their pharmacies filled opioid prescriptions their own systems had flagged. A federal jury had already found the three liable for creating a public nuisance in two Ohio counties.
cite: National Prescription Opiate Litigation, N.D. Ohio, settlements November 2022; Lake and Trumbull County verdict, November 2021

n: Mallinckrodt
d: The largest US manufacturer of generic oxycodone agreed to $1.7 billion in opioid settlement payments through its bankruptcy, having earlier paid $35 million to resolve DEA findings that it failed to report suspicious orders. Its output at one point exceeded the rest of the generic market combined.
cite: In re Mallinckrodt plc, D. Del., plan confirmed 2022; DEA administrative settlement 2017

n: Teva and Allergan
d: Teva agreed to about $4.25 billion in cash and generic naloxone supply to settle US opioid claims, and Allergan to $2.37 billion. Neither admitted wrongdoing, and the naloxone component means part of the settlement is paid in the antidote to the product.
cite: National opioid settlements announced November and July 2022

n: Indivior
d: Resolved US charges for $600 million after a subsidiary pleaded guilty to a felony over marketing an opioid dependence film as safer around children than it had evidence to claim. Its former parent paid $1.4 billion separately, and its former chief executive pleaded guilty to a misdemeanour.
cite: US v. Indivior Solutions, W.D. Va., plea July 2020; Reckitt Benckiser resolution 2019

n: The Star Entertainment Group
d: A NSW inquiry found the company unsuitable to hold its Sydney licence after evidence it disguised gambling spend as hotel expenses on China UnionPay cards and extended large credit lines to patrons whose organised-crime links had been reported internally. AUSTRAC took it to the Federal Court over 117 high-risk patrons and its dealings with the Suncity junket operator, whose Sydney turnover it put above A0 million a week; it sought A00 million. The company argued a penalty above A00 million would render it insolvent, having A8 million in cash against more than A.1 billion in debt, and was rescued by a A00 million investment. Two former senior executives admitted breaches and were penalised; the Federal Court found two more had breached their duties in 2026.
cite: Bell Review report, NSW Independent Liquor and Gaming Authority, September 2022; AUSTRAC Federal Court proceedings and penalty hearing, June 2025; ASIC proceedings against former executives, 2025-2026
rank: Casino operator — junkets and credit (casinos & junkets)

n: Tak Chun Group
d: Macau's second-largest junket operator ran under-the-table betting alongside the licensed tables, on a scale prosecutors put in the billions. Its chairman was sentenced to 14 years in April 2023 for criminal association, illegal gambling and aggravated laundering; the fraud counts were overturned on appeal.
cite: Court of First Instance, Macau SAR, April 2023; Court of Second Instance, January 2024

n: MGM Grand and The Cosmopolitan
d: Both properties entered non-prosecution agreements and forfeited $7.45 million over years of taking play from an illegal bookmaker whose income they had reason to question. A former MGM Grand president was separately convicted of failing to file the required report.
cite: US Attorney, C.D. Cal., non-prosecution agreements January 2024; US v. Sibella, conviction 2024
rank: Casinos — host and compliance staff (casinos & junkets)

n: British Columbia casinos — the Cullen Commission
d: A public inquiry found that hockey bags of $20 notes were accepted at Lower Mainland casinos for years while regulators and government knew and did not act. The commissioner declined to call it wilful blindness by individuals and located the failure in the institutions instead.
cite: Commission of Inquiry into Money Laundering in British Columbia, final report, June 2022
rank: Casino operators and the provincial regulator (casinos & junkets)

n: Aleman, Cordero, Galindo & Lee (Alcogal)
d: The firm that replaced Mossack Fonseca as the region's largest incorporator appeared throughout the Pandora Papers, having formed thousands of structures whose beneficial owners it had not verified. It says it complied with the law in force at the time; no charge has been brought.
cite: ICIJ Pandora Papers, October 2021
rank: Offshore formation agent (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: US anonymous company formation
d: Delaware, Wyoming and Nevada companies can be formed in minutes with no verified owner, and appear repeatedly in trafficking and laundering files. The Corporate Transparency Act was to end that from 2024; an interim rule in March 2025 exempted domestic companies from reporting, leaving the requirement on foreign entities only.
cite: Corporate Transparency Act 2021; FinCEN interim final rule, March 2025
rank: Corporate registry as a service (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: ANOM — Operation Trojan Shield
d: After Phantom Secure closed, the FBI and Australian police built and distributed the replacement themselves, reading roughly 27 million messages from 12,000 devices before the takedown in June 2021. More than 800 arrests followed across 16 countries; the admissibility of the material has been litigated ever since.
cite: US v. Iosif Florea et al., S.D. Cal., indictment June 2021; AFP Operation Ironside
rank: Encrypted handset network — run by police (encrypted communications)

n: Ghost
d: A platform sold with modified handsets and a remote wipe function, taken down in September 2024 with 51 arrests across Europe, Australia and North America. Its alleged administrator, who had run it from his parents' house in Sydney, was arrested there.
cite: Europol and Eurojust coordinated action, September 2024; AFP charges

n: Matrix
d: Found on a phone belonging to a man convicted of murdering a Dutch crime journalist, and taken down in December 2024 after French and Dutch investigators monitored it for three months and read 2.3 million messages. It ran on more than 40 servers and admitted users by invitation only.
cite: Europol and Eurojust, Operation Passionflower, December 2024

n: Exclu
d: Dutch and German police read the service for five months before closing it in February 2023, then raided a drug lab and two cocaine sites the messages had identified. Its operators were prosecuted in the Netherlands.
cite: Dutch Politie and Europol action, February 2023; Netherlands prosecutions from 2023

n: Ennetcom
d: The first of the European encrypted-phone takedowns: 19,000 handsets, servers seized in Canada, and an owner convicted of laundering and weapons offences. The recovered message store has been used in Dutch murder and trafficking trials for years since.
cite: Dutch Openbaar Ministerie prosecution from April 2016; Rotterdam District Court conviction

n: Grupo Wisa and Balboa Bank & Trust
d: A trading group in the Colon Free Zone, a duty-free retailer, a newspaper and a bank were designated together as a trade-based laundering network for several trafficking organisations. Panama's regulator seized the bank and wound it down; one of the designated principals later pleaded guilty in Miami to a bank-fraud conspiracy.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, May 2016; Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama seizure, 2016
rank: Free-zone trading group and its bank (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Zimbabwe gold refining and export
d: An undercover investigation recorded intermediaries, one of them an ambassador-at-large, offering to wash cash through the state gold refinery and export it as bullion. Gold turns cash into a commodity with an invoice; the government appointed a commission and the practice continued.
cite: Al Jazeera Investigative Unit, Gold Mafia, March 2023; Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe statements
rank: State refinery and licensed buyers (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Port of Algeciras
d: Spain's largest container port sits eight miles from Morocco, and the hashish and cocaine networks around it have recruited from the municipal police, the customs service and the port workforce. Successive operations there have arrested serving officers rather than only dockers.
cite: Spanish Policia Nacional and Guardia Civil operations, 2018–2024; Audiencia Provincial de Cadiz proceedings
rank: Container port and strait crossing — access control (shipping, freight & ports)

n: EU port corruption — the EUDA and WCO review
d: A joint review found more than 1,826 tonnes of drugs seized in or bound for EU ports between January 2019 and June 2024, 1,244 tonnes of it at the ports themselves and 82 percent of it cocaine, concentrated at Antwerp and Rotterdam. Its finding on the mechanism is the one the individual prosecutions show: the size of the average consignment implies significant penetration of EU ports by criminal networks, including the likely corruption of some port staff. The vulnerability is staff access, not screening technology. Antwerp alone seized 116 tonnes in 2023, a record.
cite: European Union Drugs Agency and World Customs Organization joint report, 2025; Belgian customs figures, January 2024
rank: Container terminals across the EU (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Nemesis Market
d: German police seized the market's servers in March 2024 and the US Treasury designated its administrator, an Iranian national, in a rare case of naming a market operator by name rather than only the platform. It had roughly 30,000 users and 1,000 vendors selling narcotics.
cite: BKA seizure, March 2024; OFAC designation, March 2024

n: Endo International
d: Agreed to about $450 million in opioid settlements through bankruptcy, having marketed a reformulated oxycodone as harder to abuse than the evidence supported. New York had already obtained a separate settlement over the same claims.
cite: In re Endo International plc, S.D.N.Y. bankruptcy, settlement 2022; New York State settlement 2021

n: Resorts World Las Vegas
d: Settled a Nevada Gaming Control Board complaint for $10.5 million over hosting patrons with convictions for illegal bookmaking and money laundering, including one who had been barred from the state's casinos. Its president departed before the settlement was approved.
cite: Nevada Gaming Commission settlement, 2025; Gaming Control Board complaint, 2024

n: The Manta fishing fleet
d: Fifteen Ecuador-based targets were designated on 20 August 2026 and ten fishing vessels identified as blocked property, over a network run out of Manta for Los Choneros and Los Lobos. The fleet does not carry the cocaine: it meets the go-fast boats at sea and supplies refuelling, food and medical assistance while watching for law enforcement, so a licensed vessel with a legitimate reason to be offshore becomes the service station for the crossing. Treasury noted the boats used government-subsidised fuel, which puts a state subsidy inside the cost structure of the route. One designated operator was said to coordinate 30 to 40 tonnes a month; another owned or controlled six companies, five of them in marine fishing. The Ecuadorian navy took 1.8 tonnes off a small fishing boat off Manabi in April 2026.
cite: US Treasury press release sb0610 and OFAC designations under E.O. 14059 and E.O. 13224 as amended, 20 August 2026; Federal Register notice, 25 August 2026; Ecuadorian Ministry of National Defense seizure, 1 April 2026
rank: Licensed tuna companies and ten blocked vessels (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Tapgas Mexico
d: A Culiacan gas company designated with its owner, whose organisation Treasury says had laundered at least $16.5 million for Sinaloa Cartel clients including Los Chapitos and the Zambada faction. Fuel distribution moves cash volumes that would draw attention anywhere else.
cite: OFAC designation under E.O. 14059, 2025
rank: Fuel distribution — laundering vehicle (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Los Pochos company network
d: Nine Guatemalan businesses have been designated across two actions as property of an organisation that controls trafficking on the Mexican border and supplies the Sinaloa Cartel. The companies are the part of the structure that survives a change of leadership, which is why Treasury relisted them.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, December 2019; E.O. 14059 designations, February 2024
rank: Guatemalan trading and service companies (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Afghan hawala houses — the Barakzai network
d: Two Kandahar exchange houses were designated with the opium network that used them, one belonging to the network's head and one to its main financial conduit. Hawala settles by ledger between brokers rather than by transfer, so there is no wire for a bank to screen and no correspondent to hold liable.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, 2012; Afghan Threat Finance Cell investigation
rank: Money exchange houses — value transfer (banks & money transmission)

n: Afghan and UAE trading companies — the Mohammad Din network
d: Four companies in Afghanistan and the UAE were designated as vehicles for a Helmand heroin operation running labs in Musa Qala and Sangin. Dubai's role in the Afghan opiate economy is where the proceeds are placed rather than where the drug moves.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, 2014
rank: Trading companies — proceeds placement (banks & money transmission)

n: Latakia captagon production
d: Treasury identified a facility in the coastal province run by a presidential cousin as producing 84 million captagon tablets in 2020, coordinated with the Fourth Division and Hezbollah contacts. Manufacture at that volume needs presses, precursor supply and export clearance, which is why the map treats it as industry rather than as a lab.
cite: OFAC designation under E.O. 13582, March 2023

n: Syrian private security companies
d: The EU designated several private security companies as shells for pro-regime militias involved in the drug economy. The security licence is the cover: it explains armed men, vehicles and access to sites without any of it needing to be accounted for as military.
cite: Council of the EU designations, April 2023
rank: Security firms — militia shells (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: The Joumaa exchange houses and used-car network
d: Treasury designated a Lebanese-Colombian trafficker along with nine associates and 19 businesses, describing a system that moved as much as $200 million a month through exchange houses, bulk cash and used-car sales in the United States resold in West Africa. A Virginia indictment followed, charging the coordination of at least 85 tonnes of Colombian cocaine with Los Zetas. He has never been in US custody.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, January 2011; US v. Joumaa, E.D. Va., indictment November 2011
rank: Money exchange houses and vehicle trading (banks & money transmission)

n: Operation Cedar — the luxury goods circuit
d: Simultaneous raids in France, Belgium, Germany and Italy broke a laundering circuit that converted European cocaine proceeds into watches, cars and diamonds bought in Europe and resold in the Middle East. Goods carry value across borders without a wire transfer, which is the same mechanism the gold and used-car cases show.
cite: DEA Operation Cedar, February 2016; French, Belgian, German and Italian prosecutions
rank: Luxury goods trading — value transfer (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: The Khanani money laundering organisation
d: A Karachi-based exchange group designated by Treasury as laundering for drug organisations, designated terrorist groups and Chinese and Colombian networks at once, on an estimated multi-billion-dollar annual scale. Its principal was arrested in Panama, extradited, and pleaded guilty in the United States in 2016.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, November 2015; US v. Khanani, D. Ariz., plea 2016
rank: Exchange house group — multi-client laundering (banks & money transmission)

n: Tri-border free zone trading — the Barakat network
d: Argentina froze the assets of a Ciudad del Este trading network in 2018 and the US designated its principals; the free zone's paperwork lets goods, invoices and value move without matching cargo. It sits at the junction of the Paraguayan cocaine corridor and the region's largest informal remittance market.
cite: OFAC designations 2004 and 2018; Argentine Unidad de Informacion Financiera freezing order, 2018
rank: Free trade zone import-export (banks & money transmission)

n: The eight Wuhan and Hebei chemical companies
d: Eight China-based companies and eight employees were indicted in Florida in October 2024 over synthetic opioids and fentanyl precursors, with the charges naming who held each firm's bitcoin wallet or received its Western Union payments. Five of the companies have since ceased operating and China scheduled three of the chemicals involved, which had not been controlled when the sales were made.
cite: US Department of Justice, M.D. Fla., indictments unsealed October 2024
rank: Chemical manufacture and export — sales agents and payment handlers (chemicals & precursors)

n: Hubei Aoks Bio-Tech
d: A Wuhan company, its sole director and three senior employees were charged in Los Angeles with conspiring to manufacture and distribute fentanyl and with selling precursors and xylazine worldwide. The misbranded-drug counts alongside the trafficking counts are the tell: the same shipments were being described to customs as something else.
cite: US v. Hubei Aoks Bio-Tech Co. Ltd., C.D. Cal., indictment November 2024
rank: Chemical manufacture — director and senior staff (chemicals & precursors)

n: Vasudha Pharma Chem
d: An Indian company and senior executives were indicted after selling an undercover agent 25 kilograms of a listed fentanyl precursor twice, then negotiating four tonnes of it — half destined for Sinaloa, half for the United States — for about $380,000. It had advertised the chemicals openly on its website and at trade shows.
cite: US Department of Justice and DEA, indictment announced March 2025

n: Chinese precursor vendors and crypto payment
d: Blockchain tracing puts inflows to Chinese precursor vendors at roughly $31 million in 2023, $35 million in 2024 and $39 million in 2025, with about 97 percent accepting cryptocurrency and most marketing xylazine or nitazenes alongside the precursors. A 2026 indictment of Shandong suppliers added a material-support-to-a-terrorist-organisation count, available because Mexican cartels were designated in February 2025.
cite: US indictment of Shandong-based suppliers, 2026; TRM Labs blockchain analysis, 2026
rank: Online precursor marketplaces — payment rails (chemicals & precursors)

n: Law firm escrow accounts — the Ravenell case
d: A prominent Baltimore defence lawyer was convicted after a 16-day trial of using his firm's escrow and operating accounts to move more than a million dollars in drug proceeds, pay counsel for other members of the conspiracy, and invest on a trafficker client's behalf. He was sentenced to 57 months. Escrow is the one account a lawyer can hold for a client without explaining whose money it is.
cite: US v. Ravenell, D. Md., verdict December 2021, sentence June 2022
rank: Defence counsel — client trust account (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Chinese money laundering organisations
d: Brokers who buy cartel cash in the United States at a discount and settle in China through mirror transfers have largely displaced the older Colombian peso exchange. Prosecutions in North Carolina, Georgia and Virginia have produced sentences of six to fifteen years and forfeitures in the tens of millions; the demand side is Chinese nationals needing dollars abroad, which is what makes the service cheap.
cite: US Department of Justice, W.D.N.C. sentence 2026; E.D. Va. sentences 2024–2025; DEA National Drug Threat Assessment
rank: Informal brokers — cash collection and mirror transfer (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Sham technology company — the Bibliowicz case
d: A senior executive was convicted by a Brooklyn jury of laundering more than $300 million for cartels including Sinaloa, routed behind a technology company that existed to explain the flows. He was sentenced to 12 years with a $330 million forfeiture judgment.
cite: US v. Bibliowicz Mitrani, E.D.N.Y., verdict December 2025, sentence April 2026
rank: Corporate executive — unlicensed money transmission (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: High-value freight forwarders — the jewellery corridor
d: An organisation working from a jewellery-store front in the Los Angeles Jewelry Mart shipped locked cases of cocaine to New York's Diamond District through forwarders that specialise in precious metals and fine art, and sent the cash back the same way. At least 1,300 parcels moved between the two cities. Carriers built for high-value goods offer sealed handling and few questions.
cite: US v. Rodriguez, O'Connell and others, C.D. Cal., superseding indictment 2025
rank: Specialist parcel carriers — jewellery and fine art (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Cross-border trucking brokerage
d: An Ontario investigation found a broker-style operation inside the licensed trucking sector, with drivers knowingly moving loads within legitimate supply chains; 21 people were charged with 104 offences and about 1.7 tonnes of drugs seized. Road freight has no equivalent of the port's fixed choke point, so the recruitment happens at the brokerage.
cite: Windsor Police, CBSA and Ontario Provincial Police, Project Bay, 2025–2026
rank: Commercial road freight — brokers and drivers (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Airport ground handling — the NAHCO case
d: A cargo manager at Nigeria's main aviation handling company pleaded guilty to stealing and trafficking 25 kilograms of ephedrine from the import shed inside the customs area at Lagos airport, and was sentenced to three years. Ground handling sits on the airside of every control and is rarely counted as part of the supply chain.
cite: Federal High Court Lagos, NDLEA prosecution, conviction December 2025
rank: Cargo handling company — import shed manager (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Sahel gold and real estate — laundering the cocaine surge
d: Cocaine seizures across Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania and Niger rose from an average of 13 kilograms a year between 2015 and 2020 to 1,466 kilograms in 2022, and Mauritania alone took 2.3 tonnes by mid-2023. The UN found the proceeds moving into gold and real estate, sectors growing fast enough to absorb them, and named armed groups in Mali among the beneficiaries. No prosecution has followed in any of the five states.
cite: UNODC, Drug Trafficking in the Sahel, April 2024
rank: Artisanal gold buyers and property developers (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Faria Lima funds and fintechs — Operation Carbono Oculto
d: Brazilian authorities identified some 26 billion reais of PCC money laundered over four years through investment funds and fintechs in Sao Paulo's financial district, alongside a fuel scheme covering illegal methanol imports, over a thousand petrol stations, and a port terminal, ethanol plants and a truck fleet held inside more than 40 funds. Fintechs were not then regulated as financial institutions, which is what made the transactions hard to follow. Named firms deny wrongdoing and describe themselves as used rather than complicit.
cite: Operacao Carbono Oculto, Receita Federal and Sao Paulo GAECO, from 28 August 2025
rank: Investment funds and payment fintechs (banks & money transmission)

n: The adulterated fuel chain
d: Methanol entered through the port of Paranagua on falsified paperwork, was diverted to blenders who mixed it into petrol, and reached consumers through stations the organisation controlled. Prosecutors put illicit fuel imports at 10 billion reais and retail sales at 52 billion. Buyers were defrauded twice over, on volume and on specification, which is the rare instance on this map where the laundering vehicle harms the public directly rather than only carrying the proceeds.
cite: Operacao Carbono Oculto findings, Receita Federal and ANP, 2025
rank: Fuel importers, blenders and retail stations (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: The Shimada network and the leaked raid
d: Two Brazilians, three Brazilian companies and one Portuguese company were designated on 1 July 2026 over a laundering network running between Florida and Sao Paulo. Treasury put the sum at more than $30 million generated in US cities and moved back to Brazil in cryptocurrency; the FBI had already arrested six of the Florida node in January 2026. One of the designated companies had surfaced a year earlier in a laundering network tied to a Sao Paulo football club whose agent was said to work for the PCC. What happened next is the record: Brazil's federal police had a parallel operation ready, and their chief said the uncoordinated US designation forced them to execute their warrants earlier than planned. The associate was captured; the principal escaped and is a fugitive.
cite: US Treasury press release sb0549 and OFAC designations under E.O. 14059 and E.O. 13224 as amended, 1 July 2026; FBI arrests and indictment, S.D. Fla., January 2026; Brazilian Federal Police Operation Exchange and statements by the Federal Police director, July 2026
rank: Payment and trading companies moving proceeds in crypto (crypto & digital rails)

n: The Hong Pang Group
d: Founded in 1998 with drug revenues under the privileges of a ceasefire deal, the group spread into construction, agriculture, gems and minerals, petroleum, electronics and department stores, with offices in Yangon, Mandalay and Lashio as well as Wa territory. Treasury designated 16 companies in 2005 and a further 17 with 26 individuals in 2008 as the commercial network of the United Wa State Army; US prosecutors sought $103 million in forfeitures tied to the group. It later traded under a different name and its founder remains a fugitive.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, November 2005 and November 2008; US v. Wei Hsueh Kang and others, E.D.N.Y., indictment unsealed January 2005
rank: Conglomerate — construction, mining, gems, fuel, retail (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: The Menu-Based Sanctions list — a head of state without an asset freeze
d: Haiti's former president was placed on the Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions list rather than the main blocking list, which prohibits foreign-exchange transactions and bars US financial institutions from lending to him without freezing his property outright. The distinction matters for what a designation actually does: the graduated tier reaches banking relationships while leaving assets untouched, and it is the tier chosen for a designated former head of state.
cite: OFAC Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions listing under E.O. 14059, August 2024
rank: Sanctions instrument rather than a firm (banks & money transmission)

n: ENACO — the legal coca monopoly
d: Peru's state company holds the sole legal right to buy and sell coca leaf, registering around 31,000 producers and exporting to a US firm that extracts cocaine for medical use. Researchers examining the country's main legal coca valley found the monopoly pays below what traffickers offer, so most of the crop leaves the legal channel it was designed to capture. It is the one entry on this map where the state itself is the licensed buyer of the raw material.
cite: Busnel and Manrique Lopez, International Journal on Drug Policy, 2023; ENACO producer registry
rank: State coca purchasing monopoly (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Singapore's drug-proceeds statute in practice
d: Thirty-two men were convicted in 2025 alone under the Confiscation of Benefits Act, which makes possessing or moving the proceeds of drug dealing a separate offence from trafficking. The largest single laundering sentence, 38 months within a 28-year term, concerned removing about S$1.27 million from the jurisdiction. The sums are small by the standards of every bank on this layer, and the sentences are not: the same conduct that draws a corporate fine elsewhere draws imprisonment and caning here.
cite: Singapore Central Narcotics Bureau convictions, 2024 and 2025; Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act 1992
rank: Statutory regime — possession and transfer of drug benefits (banks & money transmission)

n: The tapentadol export pipeline
d: More than 60 Indian suppliers exported roughly $130 million of tapentadol pills to West African countries that had not approved the drug, at doses above the Indian manufacturing cap. Regulators had seized one manufacturer's stock and halted production after an earlier investigation; exports of the same opioid then rose. A regulator's own reply named only two firms as approved to make tapentadol for export in 2019-2024, and neither appears among the 60. Around 30 percent of West Africa's population is estimated to use tramadol or codeine.
cite: Bellingcat and Newslaundry investigation, April 2026; CDSCO records obtained under RTI; BBC Eye investigation, February 2025

n: Online pharmacies and counterfeit pills
d: Treasury designated an Indian online pharmacy and two nationals who worked with Dominican and US traffickers to sell counterfeit pills marketed as discounted legitimate medication and filled instead with illicit fentanyl. The same online suppliers sell precursor chemicals to Mexican laboratories, so one channel serves both the finished counterfeit and the raw material for it.
cite: OFAC designations, September 2025; DEA public warning, October 2024

n: Kings Romans casino
d: Treasury designated the casino and its owner's organisation in January 2018, stating it was used to store and distribute narcotics from Myanmar's United Wa State Army and to launder the proceeds, with drug seizures in Thailand, Laos and China traced back to it since 2014. The owner denied the allegations at a press conference within days. The casino kept operating and expanding, which is the clearest single measure on this map of what a designation is worth inside a jurisdiction that will not act on it.
cite: OFAC Transnational Criminal Organizations designation, January 2018; subsequent UNODC reporting on the Golden Triangle SEZ
rank: Casino — storage, distribution and laundering (casinos & junkets)

n: The Mekong casino banking system
d: UNODC counted more than 340 licensed and unlicensed casinos across the lower Mekong by early 2022, and describes them with online gambling and stablecoin transfers as a parallel banking system handling proceeds from drug trafficking, illegal gambling and cyberfraud. The displacement is documented: enforcement against Macau's junkets moved the business into Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and the Philippines, and operations there moved it again toward border and remote areas. Treasury designations in Cambodia have reached casino complexes and two banks connected to them.
cite: UNODC, Casinos, Money Laundering, Underground Banking and Transnational Organized Crime in East and Southeast Asia, January 2024; OFAC designations in Cambodia, 2025-2026
rank: Licensed and unlicensed casinos, e-junkets (casinos & junkets)

n: BVI and Dubai shells — the Gacanin structures
d: Leaked corporate records showed a Bosnian trafficker designated by the US and by Europol partners had used British Virgin Islands and Dubai free zone companies to employ men prosecutors describe as his cartel's operatives. UAE law at the time required a local sponsor, and one was named on the filings; the sponsor's representative said she had no knowledge of narcotics or laundering. Bosnian prosecutors allege the same organisation paid politicians and worked with the head of the state security service.
cite: ICIJ analysis of leaked corporate records, August 2024; OFAC and Europol-coordinated designations with the Netherlands, France and Belgium
rank: Free zone company formation and local sponsorship (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Operation BULUT and the afterlife of seized message stores
d: Coordinated raids across several European states and Turkiye in April 2025 produced 232 arrests and more than 300 million euros in assets, worked out of Sky ECC and ANOM material years after both platforms were closed. Europol's operations deputy said the archives are still turning intelligence into action. The corollary sits in the same reporting: rather than ending encrypted communication, the takedowns fragmented it into smaller bespoke services, so each seizure buys an archive rather than a market.
cite: Europol and national authorities, Operation BULUT, April 2025
rank: Archived platform data — four dismantled services (encrypted communications)

n: The Shabu Tiangge bank accounts
d: The widow of a drug-den operator was convicted on 20 September 2022 of six counts under the Anti-Money Laundering Act and sentenced to seven to 13 years on each, with fines totalling 18 million pesos. Her personal banking manager was convicted on two counts of facilitating and given four to six years: the court found he had advised the couple how to move drug proceeds from their account to a relative's after police raided the market, and said she would not have made the transfers without his advice. The sums are small — about 1.44 million pesos across three months in 2005 and 2006 — and the point is the reach. Elsewhere on this layer institutions pay penalties and no banker is charged; here the branch manager who gave the advice went to prison, the fifth Philippine bank employee convicted of laundering.
cite: Pasig City Regional Trial Court Branch 167, joint decision of 20 September 2022, Judge Annielyn Medes-Cabelis; Anti-Money Laundering Council statement; prior convictions under RA 9165, Pasig RTC 2009, affirmed on appeal 2015
rank: A savings bank branch and its personal banking manager (banks & money transmission)

n: Tirana high-rises and coastal land
d: Albania's special prosecution issued 20 arrest warrants and seized over 100 million euros in assets, tracing cocaine proceeds into land fraud along the coastline and into high-rise towers under construction in the capital. Its seizure order records the central figure planning shipments at meetings in Spain, Monaco, Germany and Aruba, and refers to meetings with senior Albanian state officials whom it does not name. Among the implicated plots is land designated for a resort promoted by US investors.
cite: Albanian Special Prosecution (SPAK) asset seizure order and arrest warrants, 2026; BIRN analysis of the investigative file
rank: Property development and land transactions (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: The Hysa network — casinos and restaurants in Mexico
d: Treasury designated 27 individuals and entities in November 2025 over a Mexico-based laundering scheme run by an Albanian family working with the Sinaloa Cartel, washing drug proceeds through casinos and luxury restaurants in Sinaloa, Sonora and other states. Separately, an independent Albanian trafficker is alleged to have moved over $31 million through Ecuador's financial system using front companies between 2015 and 2024.
cite: OFAC designations, November 2025; Ecuadorian prosecution filings; InSight Crime analysis, 2026
rank: Casinos and restaurants — placement (banks & money transmission)

n: Sutaria, SR Chemicals and Agrat Chemicals
d: An India-based pharmaceutical chemicals supplier and his salesperson used two chemical companies to ship fentanyl precursors to Mexico and Guatemala, including N-Boc-4-Piperidone, mislabelled as safe chemicals. Both were arrested by Indian authorities in March 2025 and designated on 23 April 2026 within a 23-target action against a procurement network serving the Sinaloa Cartel. US estimates put a kilogram of the precursor at roughly 1.83 kilograms of fentanyl. Treasury's framing is the significant part: cartels now synthesise from precursors imported mainly from Asia rather than refining plant material, so the chemical broker sits where the grower used to, and the offence itself is a description on a shipping document.
cite: US Treasury press release sb0468 and OFAC designations under E.O. 14059, 23 April 2026; Indian arrests, March 2025; US Department of Justice yield estimates
rank: Pharmaceutical chemical suppliers shipping mislabelled precursors (chemicals & precursors)

n: Cartok and Carhern — the precursor brokers' companies
d: Two Sinaloa companies owned by a married pair of precursor brokers were designated in April 2026. One was linked to seizures of 1-Boc-4-Hydroxypiperidine totalling over 50 kilograms; her husband, a fentanyl and cocaine supplier with family ties to the Chapitos faction, used launderers inside the United States to collect drug payments. Both were arrested in Mexico in March 2026, a month before the designation.
cite: OFAC designations under E.O. 14059, 23 April 2026; Mexican arrests, March 2026
rank: Trading companies owned by designated brokers (chemicals & precursors)

n: Reyma and Aduaeasy — customs brokerage
d: Two firms handling importation and customs clearance were designated in the same April 2026 action for materially contributing to the proliferation of illicit drugs. The customs broker is the least visible link in the precursor chain: the chemical is legal to ship, the paperwork decides whether anyone looks at it, and the broker writes the paperwork.
cite: OFAC designations under E.O. 14059, 23 April 2026
rank: Freight forwarding and customs clearance (shipping, freight & ports)

n: The Ochoa Vasco front companies
d: Treasury designated 15 entities and nine individuals as the front network of a Colombian trafficker already listed in 2007, spanning Colombia, Mexico and the Caribbean. A Guadalajara cluster controlled by his front man included an agricultural company and three construction and property firms. The pattern recurs across this layer: the fronts are ordinary businesses in unglamorous sectors, chosen because nothing about them invites a question.
cite: OFAC designations under E.O. 12978, 2011
rank: Agriculture, construction and real estate fronts (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Chams money laundering organisation
d: Designated by Treasury in April 2019 as a laundering organisation serving trafficking groups, and issued as one of OFAC's named press charts alongside the Zheng fentanyl network and the Peralta organisation. Naming the launderer separately from the traffickers it serves is the shift this layer records: the service is a business with its own clients rather than an arm of any one cartel.
cite: OFAC designation, April 2019; OFAC counter-narcotics press chart, Chams Money Laundering Organization
rank: Peso exchange and value transfer (banks & money transmission)

n: GOLDPHARMA — the mail-order pill network
d: Designated by Treasury in May 2019 as a drug trafficking organisation running internet pharmacies that shipped controlled substances by post to buyers worldwide. It is the earliest entry on this layer treating an online pharmacy as a trafficking organisation rather than a regulatory problem, a framing the Indian counterfeit-pill designations of 2025 follow directly.
cite: OFAC designation, May 2019; OFAC counter-narcotics press chart, GOLDPHARMA Drug Trafficking Organization
rank: Online pharmacy network — mail-order controlled substances (pharmaceutical supply)

n: Dragon Secure GmbH — Kraden and Skyda
d: A Zug-registered software company operating two encrypted messaging brands was designated under the illicit-drugs order in December 2024. Registering as an ordinary Swiss programming firm with a public website is a departure from the handset-based services this map records elsewhere: the product is an app rather than a modified phone, and the company is incorporated where its clients' proceeds are banked.
cite: OFAC designation under E.O. 14059, 17 December 2024
rank: Encrypted messaging software company (crypto & digital rails)

n: Atiya S.A.S. — Medellin property
d: A Medellin real estate company incorporated in May 2020 was designated in December 2024 as controlled by a Lithuanian national listed in the same action. Its stated business is holding property on its own or leased account, which is the whole utility: a company that only owns buildings generates no transactions to examine.
cite: OFAC designation under E.O. 14059, 17 December 2024
rank: Real estate holding company (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Mexican cartel crude oil smuggling
d: Treasury issued a dedicated advisory chart in May 2025 on cartel crude oil smuggling, mapping how stolen and mislabelled Mexican crude is moved and resold across the border as a revenue stream running parallel to narcotics. The same organisations that need precursor chemicals in also need value out, and a barrel of crude launders more cleanly than a wire.
cite: OFAC counter-narcotics advisory and press chart, Mexican Cartel Crude Oil Smuggling Schemes, May 2025
rank: Fuel theft, transport and cross-border resale (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Guyana as a transshipment point — the 2025 chart
d: Treasury published a dedicated chart in June 2025 setting out how traffickers use Guyana to move cocaine toward the United States, alongside the designations of two domestic organisations, a serving police officer and Colombians running the airstrips. Publishing a country-level route chart rather than a single network diagram is unusual, and marks the point at which Guyana was treated as infrastructure rather than as a series of incidents.
cite: OFAC counter-narcotics chart, Traffickers Use Guyana as a Cocaine Transshipment Point to the U.S., June 2025
rank: Airstrips, river craft and port clearance (shipping, freight & ports)

n: The Grajales company group
d: A Valle del Cauca family's cluster of agro-industrial and holding companies sat on the sanctions list for years before being removed in December 2020. The map carries it because delisting is the part of this instrument that leaves no trace: the designation is announced with a press release, the removal appears as a line in a technical update, and the businesses resume.
cite: OFAC SDN List deletions, 2 December 2020; original SDNT designations under E.O. 12978
rank: Agro-industrial and holding companies — delisting record (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Zaron Bio-Tech (Asia) Limited
d: A chemical company registered in Hong Kong and operating out of the Shanghai region, designated in April 2018 as owned or controlled by a fentanyl trafficker indicted in North Dakota for running a continuing criminal enterprise. It produces food additives and operates factories in China, Vietnam, Thailand and Singapore, and was used to move fentanyl and analogues into the United States. Four associates were designated for laundering the proceeds through money service businesses.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, April 2018; US v. Zhang, D.N.D., indictment unsealed October 2017
rank: Food additives manufacturer — fentanyl shipment (chemicals & precursors)

n: Emerald mining fronts — the Rincon Castillo network
d: Treasury identified a Colombian organisation and its associated entities in June 2018, among them emerald mining companies and the Envigado Futbol Club. Gemstones and a football club share a property useful to the trade: both carry large cash flows whose valuation is a matter of opinion rather than record.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act identification, 5 June 2018; Congressional Research Service overview of narcotics sanctions, 2018
rank: Emerald mining and a football club (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: La Oficina de Envigado — the enforcement service
d: Designated under the Kingpin Act in June 2014, with a laundering network, an underboss and ten individuals and fourteen entities designated across the following weeks. Treasury's description is what places it here: the group supplies other criminal networks with enforcement services, debt collection, extortion and murder for hire. Eight further underbosses were designated in September, several of them coordinating from inside Colombian prisons.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, June, July and September 2014
rank: Debt collection, extortion and contract violence sold as a service (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: The Mejia Salazar laundering network
d: Designated in July 2014 with members of his network for laundering narcotics proceeds on behalf of La Oficina de Envigado, one week after that group's own designation. The sequencing is the point: the enforcement arm and its launderer were treated as separate businesses with a client relationship rather than as one organisation.
cite: OFAC designations as Specially Designated Narcotics Traffickers, 1 July 2014
rank: Laundering service to a single client organisation (banks & money transmission)

n: Los Valles organisation
d: Designated in August 2014 as one of the most prolific Central American trafficking organisations, moving cocaine north through Honduras. It sits alongside the Cachiros and the Rosenthal group already on this map: three Honduran networks designated within a year of one another, each with a legitimate business face and each connected to officials the map records separately.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, 20 August 2014
rank: Family trafficking organisation and its holdings (banks & money transmission)

n: Five companies at one Medellin address
d: Treasury designated four Colombians and five companies in May 2017 as ultimately owned or directed by a La Oficina de Envigado financier through front persons. The companies span estate planning, coffee, mining and meat trading, and all five are registered at a single office in Medellin. It was the seventh OFAC action against the same organisation, which is what the layer records: the fronts are replaced faster than they are designated.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, May 2017; OFAC press chart, Gallon Henao Brothers' Business Partners and Companies
rank: Estate planning, coffee production, mining and meat trading (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Semillanos S.A. — the Cordoba farm
d: An agricultural company based at Cerete in Cordoba, with a hacienda five kilometres out of town, designated in June 2015 as owned or controlled by a financier of La Oficina de Envigado. Farmland absorbs money in a way few assets do: the yield is variable, the inputs are cash, and the valuation depends on a harvest nobody audits.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, June 2015
rank: Agricultural company and estate (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: The Ruano Yandun fleet
d: A Narino-based organisation designated in November 2017 for moving multi-ton cocaine loads from Colombia and Ecuador through Central America and Mexico using speedboats, fishing vessels and self-propelled semi-submersibles. Treasury named it a key contributor to the rise in cocaine production in Narino, which is the department the Colombian coca figures turn on.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, November 2017
rank: Speedboats, fishing vessels and semi-submersibles (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Javier Garcia Rojas and four Colombian companies
d: Three Colombians and four companies they own or direct were designated in 2018 for links to La Oficina de Envigado and to a financier designated in 2016. Treasury's stated ground is unusual on this layer: the men were targeted for attempts to undermine joint US-Colombian investigations rather than for moving drugs or money. It was OFAC's eighth action against the same organisation since its designation on 26 June 2014, which is the pattern these Medellin entries record together — the fronts are replaced about as fast as they are named.
cite: US Treasury press release sm0289, OFAC Kingpin Act designations, 2018; La Oficina de Envigado designated 26 June 2014
rank: Companies held by men accused of obstructing the investigation (banks & money transmission)

n: The Los Gueros business network
d: Six companies and five individuals were designated in September 2013 as the business network of a Guadalajara organisation within the Sinaloa Cartel, three years after the group and its four leader brothers were listed in February 2011. Treasury's finding is the method: by using aliases and putting close family members and associates on the company deeds, the group hid its ownership interest in companies and properties for many years. The designations followed the extradition of two leaders, charged in Brooklyn over an organisation alleged to have imported more than 100,000 kilograms of cocaine between 1996 and 2008.
