The holdings include a fuel and mining company, an early instance of Treasury naming fuel as a trafficking asset.
cite: US Treasury press releases tg1043 (February 2011) and jl2170 (September 2013), OFAC Kingpin Act designations; indictment E.D.N.Y., 2009; DEA statement, 24 September 2013
rank: Six companies held through relatives and associates (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Gold bars in an Italian house
d: Proceeds from drug trafficking in France were collected at a residence in Italy and converted into gold bars and sheets, then carried on to Kosovo, Turkiye and Morocco. Investigators put at least 18 million euros through the scheme in ten months and seized about 31 million in assets across two operations. A couple is under investigation in Italy for running it. Gold crosses a border as an object rather than a transaction.
cite: Eurojust and Europol coordinated operations with French, Italian and Kosovar authorities, September 2025 and June 2026
rank: Cash-to-gold conversion and transport (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Fake invoices between France and Romania
d: A network laundering 306 million euros of drug and tax-evasion proceeds through front companies and real estate was broken up in February 2026 with thirteen arrests and 24 house searches. Invoices for services never performed moved money between the two countries and cut the taxable income at the same time, so a single false document does the laundering and the evasion together.
cite: Eurojust and Europol joint investigation team, French and Romanian authorities, action day 3 February 2026
rank: Corporate front companies and fictitious services (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: A laundering service with a client list
d: Twenty-three people were arrested in January 2025 running a scheme that had laundered around 100 million euros. Prosecutors described the group as acting as a financial service for other criminals to launder their profits, which is the distinction this layer keeps returning to: the launderer is a business with customers rather than a department inside any one trafficking group.
cite: Eurojust coordinated investigation, arrests January 2025
rank: Financial service sold to other criminal groups (banks & money transmission)

n: Shell companies for the Camorra and 'Ndrangheta
d: French, Italian and Swiss authorities followed suspicious financial movements to a laundering operation serving members of both the Camorra and the 'Ndrangheta, using shell companies, false invoicing and luxury investments to clean millions in cocaine profits. A Belgian customs seizure in late 2025 tied the money back to the shipments. Two organisations that compete in the drug market shared the same laundering service.
cite: Eurojust and Europol, French, Italian and Swiss investigation; arrest of the high-value target and six others, 2026
rank: Shell companies, false invoicing and luxury investments (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Lithuanian property and the Icelandic route
d: A group moving cocaine, MDMA, ketamine and methamphetamine into Iceland laundered the revenue through real estate and other property in Lithuania. Twenty-four arrests were made across five countries in February 2026 with 41 house searches. The quantities are small by this map's standards and the structure is not: a retail trade at one end of Europe funding a property portfolio at the other.
cite: Eurojust coordinated action day, arrests in Iceland, Lithuania, Spain, Belgium and Denmark, February 2026
rank: Real estate as the destination for retail drug revenue (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Adapted vehicles out of Brussels
d: Belgian and French authorities broke up a network in June 2026 that prepared vehicles with hidden compartments and ran consignments out of France and Belgium into Italy and Spain. Eleven arrests, 60,000 euros in cash and several vehicles seized. Europol estimates half of the most threatening criminal networks in the EU are involved in the drug trade, which is the context for treating a garage as trafficking infrastructure.
cite: Eurojust coordinated operation, Belgian and French authorities, June 2026
rank: Vehicle preparation with concealed compartments (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Vlissingen, Rotterdam and the Los Lobos consignments
d: A joint Ecuadorian, Belgian and Dutch operation dismantled a network shipping for Ecuador's Los Lobos, with seizures including 1.1 tonnes at Rotterdam in June 2025 and over three tonnes in Belgium, and sixteen arrests on the action day. It is the same corridor the Manta fishing fleet designations describe from the loading end, recorded here at the port of arrival.
cite: Europol-supported joint operation, Ecuador, Belgium and the Netherlands, 2025-2026
rank: Container terminals and importer companies (shipping, freight & ports)

n: The Belgian cocaine laboratory
d: Fourteen arrests across Belgium, Germany and Italy in April 2025, over 780 kilograms of cocaine seized and an underground laboratory dismantled. The paste was shipped from Colombia and refined inside the European Union rather than at origin, which moves a step of production across the Atlantic and puts the chemist alongside the importer.
cite: Europol-supported joint operation, Belgian and Italian authorities, April 2025

n: Scottish network logistics
d: Thirteen suspects from a Scottish organised crime group were arrested in March 2026 over the transport of hundreds of kilograms of cocaine, in an action coordinated from Eurojust rather than domestically. A domestic British group appearing on a European coordination docket is the point: the logistics arm is the part that crosses borders and so the part that draws a joint investigation team.
cite: Eurojust coordinated joint action day, 27 March 2026
rank: Transport arrangement for bulk consignments (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: OKX
d: The exchange pleaded guilty in 2025 to operating an unlicensed money transmitting business without registering with FinCEN, and agreed to pay more than $504 million. It is among the largest anti-money-laundering resolutions on record and belongs on this layer for the same reason the mixers do: a venue that moves value without identifying its users serves whoever needs that service.
cite: US guilty plea and penalty, 2025
rank: Exchange — unlicensed money transmission (crypto & digital rails)

n: KuCoin (PEKEN Global Limited)
d: A $297 million penalty for failing to implement effective anti-money-laundering measures and to report suspicious transactions, with executives separately indicted in the United States over the Bank Secrecy Act and unlicensed money transmission. The exchange was registered in the Seychelles while serving customers in jurisdictions where it was not licensed.
cite: US penalty and executive indictments, 2025
rank: Exchange — suspicious transaction reporting (crypto & digital rails)

n: The 2025 enforcement gap
d: US anti-money-laundering and sanctions penalties fell to about $1.7 billion in 2025, a 61 percent drop from $4.3 billion the year before, and for the first time in more than two decades not one US bank faced a major penalty in these categories. Enforcement shifted toward crypto and toward individual prosecutions. This layer records institutions penalised for moving drug proceeds; the year in which the banks were not penalised is part of that record.
cite: Fenergo and Kroll compilations of 2025 penalties; FinCEN and DOJ policy statements, 2025
rank: Regulatory pattern rather than a firm (banks & money transmission)

n: Paxos Trust Company
d: Fined $26.5 million by New York regulators for failing to monitor illicit flows from a partner exchange. The finding reaches the layer beneath the exchange: the issuer of the token was held responsible for what the venue distributing it did with it.
cite: New York Department of Financial Services consent order, 2025
rank: Stablecoin issuer — partner monitoring (crypto & digital rails)

n: Platinum Gaming and ProgressPlay
d: The UK Gambling Commission fined one operator 10 million pounds in October 2025 over gaps in anti-money-laundering and safer gambling controls, and another 1 million pounds in August for failing to verify player funds and monitor high-risk accounts. Regulators have said gambling operators must apply the same customer due diligence standards as banks; the fines are what the gap between the two costs.
cite: UK Gambling Commission penalties, August and October 2025
rank: Online gambling operators — source of funds checks (casinos & junkets)

n: The FATF blacklist — three countries
d: Only Iran, North Korea and Myanmar sit on the FATF list subject to a call for action, unchanged since Myanmar was added in October 2022. All three appear in this map's other layers, and the overlap is the finding: the jurisdictions the global standard-setter treats as beyond monitoring are the same ones where no official has ever been prosecuted for drug capture.
cite: FATF public statement, high-risk jurisdictions subject to a call for action, February 2026 plenary
rank: Jurisdiction-level listing rather than a firm (banks & money transmission)

n: The grey list and its exits
d: Burkina Faso, Mozambique, Nigeria and South Africa were removed from FATF's increased-monitoring list in October 2025, South Africa after only two years. Kuwait and Papua New Guinea were added in February 2026. Each of the four exits is a country this map records for capture cases or protected corridors, so a compliance clearance and a prosecution record can move in opposite directions at the same time.
cite: FATF plenary outcomes, October 2025 and February 2026
rank: Increased-monitoring listing and delisting (banks & money transmission)

n: Bolivia and the British Virgin Islands listings
d: Both were added to FATF's increased-monitoring list in June 2025, in the same session that removed Croatia, Mali and Tanzania. The pairing is instructive: a cocaine-producing state and an offshore company registry listed together, at opposite ends of the same chain.
cite: FATF plenary outcome, 13 June 2025
rank: Jurisdictions added to increased monitoring (banks & money transmission)

n: Laos and Nepal listings
d: Added in February 2025, in the session that removed the Philippines after four years of reform. Laos also holds the Golden Triangle special economic zone and the designated casino this map records separately, so the listing reaches the banking system of a state that granted the concession.
cite: FATF plenary outcome, 21 February 2025
rank: Jurisdictions added to increased monitoring (banks & money transmission)

n: Correspondent banking as the enforcement mechanism
d: When FATF names a jurisdiction, correspondent banks worldwide restrict or price in the risk regardless of whether their own regulator requires it, which is how a listing bites without any prosecution. The UAE's grey listing in 2022 and removal in 2024 moved the cost of moving money through Dubai in both directions without a single case being tried.
cite: FATF listing and delisting decisions, 2022 and 2024; correspondent banking practice
rank: Bank-to-bank relationships as a control point (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: The Akwesasne cross-border route
d: Three dual Canadian-American citizens were arrested in July 2026 over an international trafficking operation running through Akwesasne, a territory whose land crosses the US-Canada border and two Canadian provinces. The investigation required US, Canadian and tribal law enforcement to act jointly, which is the difficulty the route exploits: jurisdiction changes several times inside a few kilometres.
cite: US v. Lazore, Arquette and Ransom, N.D.N.Y., arrests 30 July 2026
rank: Territory straddling an international boundary (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Balloons over the Jordanian border
d: With Syrian production disrupted after December 2024, smugglers moved captagon south first on quadcopter drones and, when those proved expensive and low-yield, on large heavy-lift helium balloons carrying GPS guidance and timed remote-release mechanisms that drop the payload once across the border. Launching from the empty Hamad desert removed the need for inhabited areas or local help. Jordan intercepted 21 attempts from Sweida between January and July 2025 and 128 more between July 2025 and April 2026, and has struck inside Syria five times since Assad fell, most recently with F-16s against six locations on 3 May 2026. At least 46 million pills have been intercepted since mid-2025, most of them off balloons. When the state that ran a trade stops running it, the method improves rather than the volume falling.
cite: Charles Lister, Middle East Institute, data published in New Lines Magazine, May 2026; Jordanian Armed Forces 'Operation Jordanian Deterrence' statements, 3 May 2026; SANA and Arab News reporting, 14 May 2026
rank: GPS-guided helium balloons with timed release (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Sweida after the fall
d: Once a transit route for narcotics moving to Jordan and the Gulf, Sweida became the country's principal drug-trafficking centre after December 2024, with laboratories and smuggling routes held by local armed factions rather than the state. Syria's interior ministry said domestic production was virtually eradicated by late 2025 after raids on former regime facilities, and UNODC recorded fifteen industrial-scale laboratories and thirteen smaller storage sites dismantled within a year; a significant share of what now moves through Sweida arrives from Lebanon instead. Under Assad the model was centralised and industrial, tied to regime and militia structures. What replaced it is smaller, dispersed and harder to reach by conventional border enforcement — 177 million tablets were intercepted across the Arab region between December 2024 and December 2025.
cite: Middle East Eye, June 2026; UNODC research paper, December 2025; Syrian Ministry of Interior statements, late 2025; Karam Shaar Advisory analysis reported by Arab News, May 2026
rank: Production relocating from state facilities to a province (chemicals & precursors)

n: Tequila, agave and the gas stations
d: Treasury's largest single action against CJNG, on 23 July 2026, named more than fifty individuals and entities, among them sixteen legal entities designated at once under both the illicit-drugs and terrorist programmes and concentrated in Jalisco, Nayarit, Michoacán and Zacatecas. The fronts are ordinary businesses: tequila distilleries and agave producers, beverage crop companies, gas stations, a private security firm, wholesale clothing and a children's footwear store. It was coordinated with Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit and followed nearly thirty earlier actions covering more than 250 targets since 2015. The action also designated the cartel's new leader, who took over after his stepfather was killed in a Mexican government operation in February 2026 — so the network was mapped and listed faster than the leadership changed.
cite: US Treasury press release sb0573 and OFAC recent actions, 23 July 2026, under E.O. 14059 and E.O. 13224 as amended; coordinated with Mexico's Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera
rank: Agave and beverage crop production, fuel retail (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: J and C Import and Central Logistica de Servicios
d: Two Guatemala-based import and export companies designated on 23 April 2026 within a single 23-target action against a synthetic opioid procurement network tied to the Sinaloa Cartel. One received 116 kilograms of N-Boc-4-Piperidone over two months, sourced from Indian suppliers designated in the same action; the other shipped both precursors and finished fentanyl. The action names every stage at once — Indian chemical suppliers, a Guatemalan broker and his freight companies, and Mexican precursor brokers arrested a month earlier — so the supply chain is described as a chain rather than as separate national problems.
cite: US Treasury press release sb0468 and OFAC designations under E.O. 14059, 23 April 2026
rank: Guatemala City import-export firms on the precursor route (chemicals & precursors)

n: Kovay Gardens and the timeshare boiler rooms
d: A resort near Puerto Vallarta, open for more than two decades as an ordinary tourist business, designated on 19 February 2026 with five individuals and seventeen companies spanning timeshare, real estate, tourism, travel, automotive services, accounting and financial services. The model is vertically integrated: the resort sells genuine timeshares, then passes its customer database to cartel-run call centres that sell the same owners fraudulent resale and re-rental services. Between 2019 and 2023 the schemes cost roughly 6,000 American victims about $300 million. It was OFAC's sixth action against CJNG timeshare fraud, bringing the total past 90 individuals and entities, and Treasury issued a 30-day general licence to wind down dealings with the resort. Unlike almost everything else on this layer, the money is taken from the buyers rather than laundered after the fact.
cite: OFAC designations and Treasury statement, 19 February 2026, with General License authorising wind-down; prior CJNG timeshare designations from March 2023 and August 2025; investigation by FBI, DEA, IRS and CBP coordinated with Mexico's Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera
rank: Resort, call centres and 17 associated companies (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Abou Merhi Group — the Joumaa maritime network
d: Four Lebanese nationals, two Germans and eleven companies were designated in October 2015 for supporting the Joumaa organisation, which Treasury describes as a laundering ring benefiting Hezbollah. At the centre is a Lebanese holding company with subsidiaries across Africa, the Middle East and Europe, and five named vessels; the individuals were listed for their management roles rather than for handling drugs, two of them the owner's children. The vessels carried used cars for the network, which is the mechanism — value moves in the price and paperwork of goods on ships the network itself owns. Lebanese media reported in March 2016 that the family and companies had been cleared; Treasury said that was false and that all remained designated. The trafficker the action was built around, indicted in Virginia in 2011 over 85 tonnes of cocaine and more than $250 million laundered, remains a fugitive.
cite: US Treasury press release jl0196, OFAC Kingpin Act designations, October 2015, coordinated with DEA and Customs and Border Protection; Joumaa organisation designated 26 January 2011; indictment E.D. Va., November 2011; Treasury statement rebutting reports of clearance, March 2016
rank: Shipping holding company and five named vessels (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Forty investment funds and a port terminal
d: Brazilian investigators identified about forty investment funds holding roughly 30 billion reais, some $5.5 billion, used to hold PCC money: four ethanol plants, a port terminal, around 1,600 trucks and more than a thousand petrol stations across ten states. The August 2025 raids ran 14 search and arrest warrants with roughly 350 searches in eight states and blocked about 1.2 billion reais. A follow-up operation found six fintechs operating as parallel banks that had moved some 26 billion reais. Federal authorities named no individuals or companies, citing sealed proceedings. The US terrorist designations of May 2026 then attached global liability to a holding structure that Brazilian prosecutors had mapped but not yet tried.
cite: Operação Carbono Oculto, Brazilian Federal Police and Receita Federal, 28 August 2025; São Paulo state prosecutors; follow-up operation on fintech platforms, 2026; US Department of State designations, 28 May 2026
rank: Investment funds, ethanol plants, a port terminal, a truck fleet (banks & money transmission)

n: A thousand petrol stations and the fuel chain
d: Prosecutors allege the PCC controlled more than a thousand petrol stations generating some 52 billion reais in retail sales, alongside distributors, four ethanol plants and a transport fleet. Fuel appears twice more on this layer, in the Mexican crude designations and in a Sinaloa-linked company group, making it the only commodity besides drugs that three separate programmes name as a primary revenue source. It differs from the laundering entries in kind: adulterated fuel is sold to ordinary motorists, so the harm reaches people who never touch the drug trade.
cite: Operação Carbono Oculto, August 2025, and São Paulo prosecutors; US Department of State designation statement, 28 May 2026
rank: Fuel retail, distribution and ethanol production (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: The Zapata Garzon family businesses
d: Designated on 1 December 2020 under the Kingpin Act for materially assisting the Clan del Golfo, together with three relatives and associates and four companies — an engineering firm, a homes business, a distributor and a general operations company — used to launder the profits, with the relatives installed as figureheads and managers. Treasury assessed that he moved about 4,500 kilograms of cocaine in shipments during the autumn of 2018. The detail that separates this from the other front-company entries is what he did with the money: on the orders of a Clan del Golfo member, he provided campaign support and funding to mayoral candidates in several Colombian municipalities. The company layer and the official layer meet in one designation.
cite: US Treasury press release sm1197, OFAC Kingpin Act designations, 1 December 2020, coordinated with US Southern Command; State Department statement, 1 December 2020; Clan del Golfo identified under the Kingpin Act, 31 May 2013
rank: Four companies held through relatives as figureheads (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: The 2026 designation rate
d: By mid-July 2026 the administration had charged at least 291 individuals for cartel-related activity and added more than 380 Latin American individuals and entities to the sanctions list. Five criminal groups were designated foreign terrorist organisations in under seven weeks: two Brazilian groups on 5 June, an Ecuadorian gang on 1 July, and two Mexican groups on 16 July. April alone brought 172 additions and 30 vessels identified as blocked property. The pace matters for reading this layer. A designation in 2015 marked an organisation as exceptional; a designation in 2026 places it among hundreds listed the same year, and the compliance consequence has broadened faster than any adjudication behind it.
cite: Miller & Chevalier, Where FTO-Designated Cartels Operate: 2026 Update, July 2026; Hughes Hubbard sanctions summary, April 2026; State Department FTO designations of 5 June, 1 July and 16 July 2026
rank: The pace of listing, as context for the layer (banks & money transmission)

n: Chone Killers and the Ecuadorian FTO tranche
d: Designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization and Specially Designated Global Terrorist on 1 July 2026 over attacks on civilians, police and government officials including assassinations. It is the third Ecuadorian organisation designated in ten months, after Los Choneros and Los Lobos in September 2025, and it was listed separately from the parent group it split from in 2020. Ecuador now carries more designated organisations than most producing states, in a country that appeared in almost no enforcement record a decade ago.
cite: US Department of State, Terrorist Designation of Chone Killers, 1 July 2026; earlier designations of Los Choneros and Los Lobos, 4 September 2025
rank: Coastal gang designated as a terrorist organisation (shipping, freight & ports)

n: The Canaries-Azores corridor
d: A two-week operation led by the Spanish Guardia Civil and coordinated through Europol, 13-26 April 2026, worked the eastern Atlantic between the Canaries and the Azores: 11 tonnes of cocaine and 8.5 of hashish seized, eight vessels intercepted, 54 arrests. The method is staged. Mother vessels — container ships, bulk carriers, small non-commercial craft — collect in Latin America and run hundreds to thousands of nautical miles into international waters; cargo moves mid-ocean onto fast long-range boats; a final transfer puts it into small craft landing at remote Portuguese and Spanish coastline. Europol calls these fragmented maritime routes, and the fragmentation is the purpose: no single vessel or party carries the whole exposure. It is the direct answer to the port enforcement recorded elsewhere on this layer — if terminals are watched, the cargo never enters one.
cite: Europol newsroom release, Atlantic operation 13-26 April 2026, led by the Spanish Guardia Civil with Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, UK and US DEA participation
rank: Mother vessels, mid-ocean transfers and landing craft (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Eight tonnes in a banana shipment
d: 8,064 kilograms of cocaine were found on 13 July 2023 in twelve pallets of bananas shipped from Ecuador via Panama, the largest seizure in Dutch history and almost double the previous record of 4.5 tonnes. Sniffer dogs found it and a container scan confirmed it; the discovery was withheld for a month for the investigation, and no arrests had been made when it was announced. The customs chief noted that recent seizures had been much smaller, as though smugglers were spreading their risk — the fragmentation the Atlantic operation would document three years later. Dutch seizures fell from 45.5 tonnes in 2023 to about 26 in 2024, while Vlissingen rose slightly.
cite: Rotterdam Public Prosecution Service statement, 10 August 2023, seizure of 13 July 2023; Dutch customs and police annual seizure figures, January 2025
rank: Container terminal and a fruit consignment (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Dutch brokers inside Colombian supply chains
d: One of three actions Europol announced together in December 2025: a Dutch-led network embedded in Colombian supply chains, a Brazilian maritime operation and a Greek at-sea transfer group — organisers, transport and receivers taken as one chain rather than three cases. The Dutch suspect, based in Ibiza and travelling frequently, is alleged to have organised shipments with his two sons using direct access to high-level Colombian traffickers. The case first surfaced in Sky ECC material and was developed years later, which is the pattern the Sky Global entry records: the archive keeps producing prosecutions long after the takedown.
cite: Europol newsroom, three coordinated cocaine supply-chain actions, December 2025; case originating in Sky ECC material
rank: A broker with direct access to Colombian suppliers (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: The Rzeszow logistical hub
d: Twenty suspects were arrested in Czechia, Slovakia and Ukraine on 18 June 2026 over a network that bought methamphetamine in Western Europe, moved it through Czechia to a logistical hub at Rzeszow in Poland, then on to Slovakia for distribution and to Uzhhorod in western Ukraine. Investigators put the traffic at about 50 kilograms of methamphetamine and two of cocaine, close to 950,000 euros in proceeds from the methamphetamine alone. The group ran separate units for procurement, transport, distribution and financial flows, and changed concealment methods continuously, carrying loads in passenger cars and buses. The direction is the finding: almost every route on this map runs toward Western Europe, and this one runs out of it.
cite: Europol and Eurojust press releases, 7-8 July 2026, on the joint investigation team of Czech, Slovak and Ukrainian authorities; action day 18 June 2026
rank: Poland as a staging point on a west-to-east corridor (encrypted communications)

n: Constructora FR de Venezuela
d: A real estate construction company with offices in Caracas and Puerto La Cruz, designated on 13 September 2012 with its founder, director and majority shareholder. Treasury described him moving significant quantities of cocaine each year by aircraft from Venezuela to Africa and by sea from Ecuador to Mexico, and laundering the proceeds through the Venezuelan economy. He had been indicted in the Southern District of Florida in December 2011, and was arrested in Panama City and handed to US authorities the day after the designation. It is the earliest Venezuelan company on this layer and it predates by thirteen years the designation of the network the state itself is now said to run.
cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation and notice, 13 September 2012; indictment S.D. Fla., 13 December 2011; arrest in Panama City and transfer to US custody, 14 September 2012
rank: Real estate construction company, Caracas and Puerto La Cruz (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: The Tren de Aragua support network
d: Designated a foreign terrorist organisation in February 2025, its leaders sanctioned in June and July, and a network of individuals and entities designated in December for providing material support. The sequence is the standard shape of a designation campaign: the organisation first, then the people, then the businesses that carry the money.
cite: US Department of State FTO designation, 20 February 2025; OFAC designations, June, July and December 2025
rank: Individuals and entities providing material support (banks & money transmission)

n: Six states, one refusal, one contrary vote
d: After the United States listed the Venezuelan military network, Ecuador and Paraguay declared it a terrorist organisation in August 2025 and Argentina, Peru and the Dominican Republic followed. Colombia's president said the cartel does not appear in any of the country's drug investigations and called it an invention; on 17 September 2025 the opposition-majority Senate voted, after an intense debate, to declare it a terrorist organisation anyway and urged the president to honour Colombia's treaty commitments. Academics have also questioned the label, noting that a cartel by definition sets prices and regulates trade. The same body of evidence produced designations in six countries, a refusal in one government and a contrary vote in that government's own legislature.
cite: National designations by Ecuador, Paraguay, Argentina, Peru and the Dominican Republic, 2025; Colombian Senate plenary proposition, 17 September 2025, and presidential statements, September 2025; US State Department FTO designation announced 16 November 2025, effective 24 November
rank: National designations following the US listing (banks & money transmission)

n: Strikes on vessels at sea
d: On 2 September 2025 the US military struck a vessel said to be carrying drugs from Venezuela, killing eleven people reported to be Tren de Aragua members; strikes continued through September, October and December, and in early October the United States declared itself in an armed conflict with drug cartels. A Senate bill requiring congressional approval for further strikes was defeated on 8 October, and the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called for an investigation on 31 October. Every other maritime record on this layer ends in a seizure, a crew list and a court file. These end with none of the three.
cite: Congressional Research Service, Venezuela: Political Crisis and U.S. Policy (IF10230), updated 2025-2026; UN High Commissioner for Human Rights statement, 31 October 2025; US Senate vote, 8 October 2025
rank: Military strikes replacing interdiction (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Oil licences alongside the designations
d: Treasury revoked and then granted a restricted licence to a US oil major in 2025, reportedly halving what it could export, then in July permitted its joint ventures to resume operations while barring cash payments to the Venezuelan government. The Cartel de los Soles was designated a global terrorist in July 2025 and a foreign terrorist organisation in November. Three days after Maduro's capture on 3 January 2026, an announced energy deal had the United States market and sell Venezuelan oil into US-controlled accounts, with roughly $3 billion in sanctioned oil to be handed over; OFAC has issued new licences to other companies and is reported to be weighing an expanded one. The layer records companies barred from the American financial system; here the same authority admits others to a market it has named as narco-terrorist.
cite: Congressional Research Service, Venezuela: Overview of U.S. Sanctions Policy (IF10715) and Venezuela: Political Crisis and U.S. Policy (IF10230), 2025-2026
rank: Export licences issued into a designated market (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Grupo MBS and the Maputo Shopping Centre
d: Three businesses were designated on 1 June 2010, the same day President Obama identified their owner as a Mozambican drug kingpin: a family-owned conglomerate, a retail store and a shopping mall in the capital. He was among the country's most prominent businessmen, with reported links to the ruling party. The designation reached him through commerce rather than a court: within a month three banks had closed their branches inside his shopping centre, which is the correspondent-banking effect operating at street level. He was never prosecuted, and in 2014 was abducted at gunpoint from the shopping centre's own yard. Mozambique's protected heroin corridor, recorded separately on this map, ran through the same years.
cite: US Treasury press release TG-729 and OFAC Kingpin Act designations, 1 June 2010; Presidential identification, 1 June 2010; State Department International Narcotics Control Strategy Report, 2010; Mail & Guardian, July 2010; reporting on the 2014 abduction
rank: Family conglomerate, a retail store and a shopping mall (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Botanica 2000 — a pharmacy making pills
d: A chemist running clandestine laboratories in Guadalajara obtained precursors for the Chapitos faction and used his own pharmacy to produce fentanyl-laced pills for shipment to the United States. OFAC's own listing files the company under retail sale of pharmaceutical and medical goods, cosmetics and toilet articles — the designation and the trade classification describe the same premises. He was arrested at Madrid airport in November 2025, detained immediately after passport control off a flight from Mexico City, and designated on 23 April 2026 in the same 23-target action as the Indian suppliers and the Guatemalan freight companies. A licensed outlet is both a legitimate purchaser of chemicals and a plausible place for pills to exist.
cite: US Treasury press release sb0468 and OFAC designations under E.O. 14059 and E.O. 13224 as amended, 23 April 2026; arrest in Madrid, November 2025
rank: Licensed retail pharmacy used as a pill press (chemicals & precursors)

n: Narco-subs and covert airstrips off Guyana
d: Four Guyanese and two Colombian nationals were designated on 5 June 2025 after an ICE Homeland Security Investigations inquiry: two men Treasury says run the largest trafficking organisations in the country, two Colombians managing clandestine airstrips, a serving police officer accused of arranging safe passage for Mexican and Venezuelan traffickers, and a former officer wanted over the abduction of a policeman in 2024. Semi-submersibles carry loads from Guyanese and Surinamese ports across the Atlantic; cocaine has been found buried in underground bunkers on airstrips and in the jungle, with Barima-Waini a recurring location. In March 2025 a cargo vessel out of Guyana was stopped off Trinidad with about 182 kilograms aboard, the packages stamped with a Toyota logo used by the Sinaloa Cartel. Treasury noted that Guyana is a close US partner and that the State Department nonetheless treats corruption there as a significant obstacle.
cite: US Treasury press release sb0156 and OFAC designations, 5 June 2025; ICE HSI New York investigation; State Department International Narcotics Control Strategy Report, 2025
rank: Semi-submersible vessels and clandestine airfields (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Kok An and the Prince Group compounds
d: Cambodia's scam-compound economy has drawn two overlapping designation lines. A sitting Cambodian senator and his network were designated in April 2026; two months later, on 23 June, nine people and 26 entities were added to the Prince Group listing, itself designated in October 2025 with 146 individuals and entities alongside the United Kingdom. Its founder was indicted in Brooklyn, had advised two Cambodian prime ministers, and was stripped of his citizenship and sent to China in January 2026. The compounds hold trafficked workers under debt bondage to run investment fraud; Treasury cited at least $10 billion lost by Americans to Southeast Asian scam operations in 2024. It belongs beside the Mekong casino entries because the same premises serve both: floors that move value without a bank record, and fraud operations upstairs.
cite: OFAC designations under E.O. 13581 as amended, 23 June 2026 (Treasury release sb0538) and 14 October 2025; designation of Senator Kok An and network, 23 April 2026; US v. Chen Zhi, E.D.N.Y. indictment unsealed October 2025
rank: Senator's companies and a scam-compound network (casinos & junkets)

n: Fictitious trading and the HK$8.9 billion file
d: Hong Kong Customs identified a laundering operation running about HK$8.9 billion through fictitious trading activity, announced in December 2025, alongside a separate syndicate handling HK$2.6 billion broken up in September. The instrument is the Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance, which criminalises dealing with property a person had reasonable grounds to believe was crime proceeds — a lower threshold than proving knowledge, and the reason company accounts rather than individuals carry the charge here.
cite: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department announcements, 16 September and 23 December 2025; Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance, Cap. 455
rank: Trading companies invoicing goods that never moved (lawyers, brokers & formation agents), Hong Kong

n: Personal bank accounts after a narcotics seizure
d: Two Customs files traced HK$53 million and HK$61 million of suspicious transactions through the personal accounts of people already arrested in drug cases, the money moving through ordinary retail banking rather than any corporate structure. Customs pairs each announcement with a warning that lending an account to move money from unknown sources is itself the offence, which is what the layer records: the smallest available laundering unit is a person with a bank card.
cite: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department announcements, 20 November 2024 and 23 May 2025
rank: Individual accounts used as laundering channels (banks & money transmission), Hong Kong

n: The Chinese money laundering organisation model
d: Six defendants pleaded guilty to laundering more than $92 million, largely proceeds of drugs imported through Mexico. The structure explains why these networks displaced older methods: Chinese nationals wanting to move money out of China buy cartel dollars already in the United States, so the cash never crosses a border and no wire is sent. The final three pleas were entered in July 2025.
cite: US Department of Justice and IRS Criminal Investigation, guilty pleas concluding July 2025
rank: Brokerage matching cash holders to currency buyers (banks & money transmission)

n: The Anbar underground and the Syrian border
d: Captagon seizures rose about 3,380 percent between 2019 and 2023, with more than four tonnes taken in 2023 alone and 17,500 kilograms found buried in Anbar in 2024; a single day in May 2024 produced 2.5 million pills. Most of it crosses a 600-kilometre border with Syria. Iraq has built the apparatus around it — a national narcotics authority since 2017, a 2023-2025 strategy, mandatory drug testing for government employees — and the country has moved from transit route to production site while that was happening. The state's own institutions are the test case: testing was extended to teachers and officials, which is an admission about where the trade had reached.
cite: UNODC seizure data 2019-2023; Iraqi Ministry of Interior announcements, May 2024 and 2025; New Lines Institute analyses, 2026
rank: Border crossings and storage on a 600km frontier (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: The Maraya and Alwefaq Ltd
d: Treasury designated a Libyan operator, two associates, a Malta-based company and the vessel itself for smuggling fuel out of Libya and moving drugs through it to Malta, running between the port of Zuwarah and Hurd's Bank just outside Maltese territorial waters, a known transfer point for illicit maritime cargo. The finding worth recording is the paperwork: he kept all official documentation clear of his name while organising the operation. The company is the registered owner and he is not on it.
cite: US Treasury press release sm1083 and OFAC designations under E.O. 13726, 2020
rank: A vessel and a Malta-registered company (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Subsidised fuel and the two governments
d: Fuel is bought by Libyan authorities at international prices, sold domestically at a heavy subsidy — official price around 0.15 dinars a litre against two or three on the black market — and resold abroad. Crisis Group's assessment is that the racket helps hold the peace between rival elites in Tripoli and Benghazi, both of which tap the unofficial income. Security Council measures allow interdiction if the designated Libyan government contact signals a cargo is suspect; no such signal has arrived in years, which the analysis attributes to the complicity of government agencies and their political bosses. The instrument exists and the state that must trigger it is the beneficiary.
cite: International Crisis Group, Watch List 2026 Spring Edition, March 2026; UN Security Council Resolutions 2146 (2014) and 2362 (2017)
rank: State fuel subsidy resold abroad (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Maltese and Libyan oil brokers
d: Six individuals, 24 entities and seven vessels were designated in 2018 for smuggling Libyan oil to Europe, the designees Maltese, Libyan and Egyptian. It belongs beside the drug records rather than apart from them: the same routes, ports and vessels carry both, and Treasury's Libya designations reach fuel and narcotics through one executive order.
cite: US Treasury press release sm0298 and OFAC designations under E.O. 13726, 2018
rank: Brokers, companies and vessels moving Libyan oil (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Execution as the enforcement instrument
d: Saudi Arabia executed 330 people in 2024, up from 172 the year before and 196 in 2022, a large share for drug offences; Amnesty recorded 37 executions for drug crimes in a single month, 34 of them foreign nationals from Egypt, Ethiopia, Jordan, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia and Syria. The kingdom is the destination market for the captagon this map tracks from Syria and Lebanon through Jordan and Iraq. The record at the receiving end consists almost entirely of executed couriers, most of them foreign; no Saudi official appears in any adjudicated case on this layer. Severity and capture reach different people.
cite: Amnesty International execution figures, 2025; Reprieve compilation verified by Reuters; Saudi Ministry of Interior and Saudi Press Agency announcements, 2024-2026
rank: Capital punishment applied to couriers (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Captagon plants in Khartoum and Blue Nile
d: Manufacturing facilities have been identified at Khartoum, Blue Nile and Jabal Awliya, with both foreign and domestic actors involved, and Kassala has become a trafficking hub with product entering through the eastern borders and the Red Sea ports. The Rapid Support Forces and Darfur rebel movements are implicated in the trade. Captagon's appeal here is the same as everywhere on this map: it mimics legal medicine closely enough to be disguised as one. Sudan scores 8.50 on state-embedded actors and produces no adjudicated case at all.
cite: GI-TOC Organized Crime Index country profile for Sudan, 2025; ENACT Africa reporting
rank: Manufacturing sites and a Red Sea entry corridor (chemicals & precursors)

n: The tramadol chain from India through Kinshasa
d: Shipments originate with Indian manufacturers and travel through the Democratic Republic of Congo before reaching the Central African Republic, where high-dose tablets are distributed under a local name meaning the cocaine of the poor. Miners at the gold operations take it to work long hours and fighters take it in combat. University research has linked rising consumption to a near-20 percent increase in deaths from fighting over mining areas, around 500 in a year. It is the same legal-pharmaceutical origin as the Indian export records on this layer, arriving at the opposite end of the chain.
cite: Wall Street Journal reporting, 12 July 2026; Uppsala University research on tramadol consumption and mining violence; GI-TOC Central Africa Observatory, June 2026
rank: Pharmaceutical shipments repurposed as a stimulant (pharmaceutical supply)

n: Gold, timber and a fuel monopoly
d: Illicit gold exports are estimated at $180 million a year, moved abroad on military cargo aircraft registered in the country and laundered through UAE-linked exporters, with a government-backed fuel monopoly generating a further $17.5 to $30 million in unjustified profits annually. The drug revenue is the smaller line and the one that buys weapons. GI-TOC's assessment is that high-ranking political and military figures, co-opted criminal actors and transnational groups have aligned to consolidate control over the country's criminal markets.
cite: GI-TOC Central Africa Observatory report, June 2026; Wall Street Journal reporting, July 2026
rank: Extractive revenue alongside the drug trade (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Standard Chartered
d: Penalised repeatedly by US and UK authorities over sanctions and anti-money-laundering failures, with settlements in 2012 and again in 2019 totalling well over a billion dollars, and a deferred prosecution agreement extended three times because the monitor kept finding the controls inadequate. The failures were in the correspondent channel that trade-based laundering depends on.
cite: US Department of Justice deferred prosecution agreements, 2012 and 2019; UK Financial Conduct Authority final notice, April 2019
rank: Correspondent and trade bank (banks & money transmission)

n: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
d: Paid A$700 million, then the largest civil penalty in Australian corporate history, after admitting more than 53,000 breaches of anti-money-laundering law. A software update disabled the automatic reporting on its intelligent deposit machines and the failure went unnoticed for three years, during which syndicates fed cash through them in structured amounts.
cite: AUSTRAC v Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Federal Court of Australia, settlement June 2018
rank: Retail bank — deposit machines (banks & money transmission)

n: Raiffeisen Bank International
d: Subject to European Central Bank supervisory pressure and US scrutiny over its Russian and eastern European exposure and its correspondent relationships. No penalty has been imposed for drug-proceeds laundering specifically. It is on this map because Vienna is the regional correspondent hub for the Balkan corridor and the supervisory record is open rather than closed.
cite: European Central Bank supervisory requirements, 2023-2024; US Treasury correspondence reported by the bank in filings
rank: Regional and correspondent bank (banks & money transmission)

n: Nordea and SEB — the Baltic branches
d: Both were found by journalists and by Baltic regulators to have processed very large non-resident flows through Estonian and Latvian branches during the same period as Danske. Swedish and Estonian regulators fined and censured the successor entities. The flows were mixed-origin; the share attributable to narcotics has never been separated out and this map does not claim it.
cite: Swedish Finansinspektionen and Estonian Finantsinspektsioon decisions, 2019-2020; European Banking Authority review
rank: Nordic banks — Baltic branch networks (banks & money transmission)

n: Pilatus Bank
d: Its licence was withdrawn after its owner was arrested in the United States; he was convicted in 2021 of running a scheme to evade Iran sanctions through the bank. Malta's failure to act on earlier warnings was one of the findings that put the country on the FATF grey list in 2021.
cite: US v. Sadr Hashemi Nejad, S.D.N.Y., conviction 2020 (later vacated on prosecutorial grounds); European Central Bank licence withdrawal, November 2018; FATF plenary decisions

n: Versobank
d: Licence withdrawn by the European Central Bank on the Estonian regulator's proposal for long-running and serious anti-money-laundering failures across a largely non-resident client base. It is the second Baltic bank closed by supervisors within months, the other being ABLV, and together they mark the point at which the Baltic non-resident channel was shut by regulators rather than by courts.
cite: European Central Bank licence withdrawal decision, March 2018; Estonian Finantsinspektsioon findings

n: Exchange houses in the OFAC designations
d: Successive OFAC actions have designated Gulf-based exchange houses moving funds for sanctioned and trafficking networks, alongside the Afghan hawala designations already on this map. The UAE was itself grey-listed by FATF from 2022 to 2024. Dubai's role as the settlement point for several networks mapped elsewhere here rests on this infrastructure.
cite: US Treasury OFAC designations, 2021-2024; FATF plenary listings, March 2022 and February 2024
rank: Money exchange and hawala houses (banks & money transmission)

n: The black market peso exchange
d: Not a company: the oldest and still the largest mechanism for repatriating US drug proceeds, in which the dollars are sold to importers who need them and the peso equivalent is paid to the trafficker at home. Nothing crosses a border as money. It has survived every generation of anti-money-laundering rules because the transactions on each leg are ordinary trade.
cite: US Treasury FinCEN advisories on trade-based money laundering; UNODC and GAFILAT typology reporting
rank: Trade-based value transfer mechanism (banks & money transmission)

n: Correspondent de-risking in the Caribbean
d: Global banks have withdrawn correspondent relationships from small Caribbean jurisdictions faster than from anywhere else, on compliance-cost grounds. The consequence is that legitimate remittance and trade flows move to less transparent channels, while the trafficking flows the withdrawal was meant to address were never dependent on those relationships in the first place.
cite: IMF and World Bank correspondent banking withdrawal reporting; Caribbean Financial Action Task Force statements; Financial Stability Board reviews

n: Suex OU
d: The first cryptocurrency exchange ever designated by OFAC. Treasury found that more than forty per cent of its known transaction history involved illicit actors, including darknet market and ransomware proceeds. Nominally Czech-registered, operationally Russian.
cite: US Treasury OFAC designation, September 2021

n: Chatex
d: Designated two months after Suex as a successor operation sharing infrastructure with it, along with three supporting companies in Latvia and Estonia. The pattern of a designated exchange reappearing under a new name within weeks is the central enforcement problem in this sector.
cite: US Treasury OFAC designation, November 2021
rank: Crypto exchange and messaging bot (crypto & digital rails)

n: Blender.io and Sinbad.io
d: Blender was the first mixer designated by OFAC, in May 2022; it shut down and reappeared as Sinbad, which was designated in turn in November 2023 and taken down by Dutch and Finnish police. Mixers are the point at which darknet drug proceeds and state-sponsored theft proceeds use the same rails.
cite: US Treasury OFAC designations, May 2022 and November 2023; Dutch FIOD and Finnish NBI takedown, November 2023

n: Genesis Market
d: Taken down in April 2023 by an operation across seventeen countries and simultaneously designated by OFAC. It sold the account access used to move and cash out proceeds rather than the drugs themselves, which is why it belongs in this layer: the laundering supply chain has its own market.
cite: Operation Cookie Monster, Europol coordination, April 2023; US Treasury OFAC designation, April 2023

n: Bohemia, Cannabia and Monopoly
d: Three of the largest remaining darknet drug markets, closed between 2023 and 2024 by Dutch, German and US operations. Monopoly's takedown fed Operation SpecTor, which produced 288 arrests across nine countries — the largest darknet drug enforcement action recorded.
cite: Dutch Politie and Openbaar Ministerie announcements, 2023-2024; Europol Operation SpecTor, May 2023; German BKA operations

n: Huione Guarantee
d: A messaging-based marketplace where laundering, stolen data and fraud services were bought with a parent company acting as escrow, processing tens of billions of dollars before it announced its own closure in May 2025 following the FinCEN action against its parent. It sat at the junction of the compound fraud economy and the regional drug proceeds channel.
cite: FinCEN section 311 final rule on Huione Group, May 2025; Elliptic and Chainalysis transaction analysis

n: Dollar stablecoin settlement in Southeast Asia
d: UNODC's 2024 regional assessment identified a dollar stablecoin on a low-fee chain as the preferred settlement instrument for Southeast Asian laundering networks and compound operators, moving value between the fraud economy, the underground banking system and the drug proceeds channel. Issuers have frozen substantial balances at law enforcement request and no enforcement action has been taken against any of them. The finding is about what the instrument is used for, not about who issues it.
cite: UNODC Casinos, Money Laundering, Underground Banking and Transnational Organized Crime in East and Southeast Asia, January 2024
rank: Dollar-denominated stablecoin on a low-fee chain (crypto & digital rails)

n: Cryptex and PM2BTC
d: Designated by OFAC and named in US indictments in September 2024 as part of a Russian-based cash-out infrastructure; servers were seized in coordination with Dutch authorities. The same operation named an individual as a laundering broker for multiple criminal categories rather than for one trade.
cite: US Treasury OFAC and FinCEN actions, September 2024; US Department of Justice indictments; Dutch police server seizures
rank: Exchange and payment processor (crypto & digital rails)

n: Samourai Wallet
d: Its founders were charged in April 2024 with conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money transmitting business and to launder proceeds, over a coin-mixing feature. The case is the sharpest test in this layer of where a software tool ends and a money services business begins, and it is unresolved.
cite: US v. Rodriguez and Hill, S.D.N.Y., indictment April 2024
rank: Non-custodial wallet and mixing service (crypto & digital rails)

n: The container lines
d: The world's largest carriers appear repeatedly as the vessel owner in multi-tonne seizures and are almost never charged, because the load is inserted and extracted by shore-side crews without the line's knowledge. Several have joined port-security partnerships and fund scanning. The entry records where the volume physically travels, not an allegation against the carriers.
cite: Europol and World Customs Organization port security reporting; national seizure records; industry security programme documentation

n: Terminal IT and planning contractors
d: Dutch and Belgian prosecutions have convicted IT contractors and terminal planners of supplying PIN codes and manipulating stack positions so that extraction crews could find a specific box among millions. It is the most technically specific corruption vector in the European chain and the hardest to screen for, because the access is legitimate.
cite: Rotterdam and Antwerp court judgments, 2021-2024; Dutch Openbaar Ministerie reporting
rank: Container terminal software and planning staff (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Airport ground handling
d: Prosecutions across European and West African airports have charged ground handlers, cleaners and catering staff with moving product past the security line. The Nigerian conviction already on this map is the pattern's clearest example; the European cases are its mirror at the receiving end.
cite: Spanish, French and Belgian prosecution records, 2020-2024; Europol airport security reporting
rank: Ramp, catering and baggage staff (shipping, freight & ports)

n: The Colon Free Zone
d: The largest free zone in the Americas and the second largest in the world, through which goods pass without entering Panamanian customs territory. Both the trade-based laundering literature and multiple OFAC designations, including one already on this map, run through it. Panama has tightened beneficial-ownership rules; the volume has not fallen.
cite: FATF and GAFILAT free trade zone typologies; US Treasury OFAC designations; Panamanian Superintendency reporting

n: The rip-on rip-off mechanism
d: The dominant method in the Atlantic cocaine flow: the load is inserted into a legitimate container at origin without the exporter's knowledge and removed at destination before customs clearance. It requires no complicity from the shipper and no falsified paperwork — only physical access at both ends. It is why port employment screening, not manifest analysis, is where the enforcement effort concentrates.
cite: Europol EU SOCTA 2025; Belgian and Dutch customs technical reporting
rank: Container insertion and extraction (shipping, freight & ports)

n: Semi-submersible construction
d: Purpose-built low-profile and fully submersible vessels are constructed in mangrove yards on the Pacific coast, each carrying several tonnes. Colombian and Ecuadorian forces seize them regularly; the builders are occasionally charged. The design has improved steadily across two decades, including transatlantic-capable hulls recovered in Europe.
cite: Colombian Armada Nacional and Ecuadorian Fuerzas Armadas seizure records; Spanish Guardia Civil recovery of a transatlantic vessel, 2019 and 2023

n: Wuhan Yuancheng Gongchuang Technology
d: One of the earliest Chinese firms indicted in the United States over fentanyl and precursor exports, charged alongside individuals in a 2018 case that described a marketing operation with English-language sales staff and multiple domain names. The company continued to appear in later enforcement reporting under related names.
cite: US Department of Justice indictment, 2018; US DEA and Congressional-Executive Commission on China reporting

n: Acetic anhydride diversion
d: The essential reagent for converting morphine to heroin has no substitute and large legitimate uses. INCB tracks the licit trade and repeatedly reports diversions in transit through Turkiye, Central Asia and the Gulf toward Afghan laboratories. It is the single chokepoint in the opiate chain where a control regime already exists and still fails.
cite: INCB Precursors report, annual; UNODC Afghan Opiate Trade Project

n: Laboratory equipment suppliers
d: Dutch and Belgian prosecutors have charged suppliers of industrial reactors, tabletting machines and glassware with knowingly equipping synthetic drug production sites in the border region. The equipment is unrestricted and has ordinary industrial buyers, so the charge turns on knowledge rather than on the goods.
cite: Dutch Openbaar Ministerie and Belgian federal prosecution filings, 2020-2024; EMCDDA/EUDA production reporting
rank: Reactor vessels, tabletting and glassware (chemicals & precursors)

n: Johnson & Johnson
d: Agreed to pay $5 billion over twenty-five years as part of the $26 billion national opioid settlement, and separately $230 million to New York. Its Tasmanian poppy operations supplied a large share of the narcotic raw material used by other manufacturers, which is the part of its role least visible in the settlement documents.
cite: National Opioid Settlement agreement, 2021; New York Attorney General settlement, June 2021
rank: Manufacturer and active ingredient supplier (pharmaceutical supply)

n: McKinsey & Company
d: Paid $573 million to states in 2021 over advice to Purdue on how to 'turbocharge' oxycodone sales, then a further $650 million to the US Department of Justice in December 2024 under a deferred prosecution agreement, with a former partner pleading guilty to obstruction for deleting records. A consultancy is on this map because the strategy documents were the product.
cite: State attorneys general settlement, February 2021; US Department of Justice deferred prosecution agreement, December 2024

n: Publicis Health
d: Paid $350 million to settle claims that it designed and ran the marketing campaigns behind opioid prescribing growth, including targeting materials for individual prescribers. The first advertising group to settle in this litigation.
cite: Multistate attorneys general settlement, February 2024

n: Kroger, Albertsons and the grocery pharmacies
d: Settled state and local opioid claims for roughly $1.4 billion and $224 million respectively, following the larger settlements by the three national chains already on this map. Dispensing data showed sustained volumes in counties where the prescription rate exceeded the population.
cite: Multistate settlement agreements, 2023; ARCOS dispensing data cited in In re National Prescription Opiate Litigation

n: Entain
d: Paid £585 million under a deferred prosecution agreement with HMRC over bribery in its former Turkish business, the largest such settlement in UK history, alongside a separate £17 million regulatory penalty for social responsibility and anti-money-laundering failures. Online gaming accounts are a standing route for layering small amounts at scale.
cite: UK Crown Court deferred prosecution agreement, 2023; UK Gambling Commission regulatory settlement, August 2022
rank: Online betting and gaming group (casinos & junkets)

n: SkyCity Entertainment Group
d: Agreed a NZ$4.16 million penalty with New Zealand's financial intelligence unit and separately faced Australian proceedings over its Adelaide casino, in both cases for failing to monitor high-value play. New Zealand pays the highest methamphetamine prices in the world and the casino floor is where that cash surfaces.
cite: New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs civil proceedings settlement, 2024; AUSTRAC v SkyCity Adelaide, Federal Court of Australia

n: The Philippine offshore gaming operators
d: Licensed offshore operators grew into a sector employing tens of thousands, then were found to host fraud compounds and laundering operations; the president ordered the entire sector shut down by the end of 2024. One licensee's operations were linked to a serving mayor later found to be a foreign national. The shutdown displaced the operations rather than ending them.
cite: Philippine Presidential directive, July 2024; PAGCOR licence revocations; Philippine Senate committee hearings, 2024

n: Trident Trust and Asiaciti Trust
d: Two of the largest offshore providers in the Pandora Papers, administering structures for clients including sanctioned and criminally implicated figures. Asiaciti was fined by Singapore's regulator for anti-money-laundering failures. Neither has been charged over drug proceeds; both supply the layer of the chain where ownership stops being traceable.
cite: ICIJ Pandora Papers, October 2021; Monetary Authority of Singapore composition penalty, 2021
rank: Offshore trust and corporate services (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Citizenship and residence by investment
d: Programmes selling citizenship or residence for investment have been used by figures under sanction or investigation to acquire travel documents and banking access. The European Commission opened infringement proceedings against Malta and the European Court of Justice ruled against the scheme; five Caribbean states came under joint US and EU pressure to tighten theirs. The mechanism is legal and the due diligence is the whole of the control.
cite: European Commission infringement proceedings and CJEU judgment, 2025; US-EU-UK joint statements on Caribbean CBI programmes, 2023-2024
rank: Passport and residence programmes (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: The Dubai free zones
d: Free zone companies can be formed with beneficial ownership visible only to the zone authority. Investigative reporting has repeatedly traced structures used by sanctioned and trafficking-linked figures to these registries, and the UAE's FATF grey listing between 2022 and 2024 turned on beneficial-ownership access. The registries were reformed rather than opened.
cite: FATF plenary decisions, March 2022 and February 2024; Dubai Unlocked and related investigative reporting, 2024
rank: Free zone company formation (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Football clubs as laundering vehicles
d: European prosecutors have charged organised crime figures with acquiring or funding lower-division clubs and using transfer fees and sponsorship to move proceeds. Spanish, Italian and Belgian cases all describe the same structure. Transfer valuations are subjective, cross-border and settled between private parties, which is what makes them useful.
cite: Spanish Fiscalia Anticorrupcion and Belgian federal prosecution filings, 2018-2024; Europol financial crime reporting
rank: Sports clubs and player transfers (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)

n: Glencore
d: Pleaded guilty in the United States and the United Kingdom to bribery and market manipulation and paid penalties totalling around $1.5 billion, with a further Swiss conviction in 2024. Its West African and Latin American oil operations sat in the same jurisdictions and used the same intermediaries as the laundering infrastructure mapped elsewhere here; the convictions are for corruption, not narcotics.
cite: US Department of Justice and CFTC resolutions, May 2022; UK Serious Fraud Office conviction and sentencing, 2022-2023; Swiss Office of the Attorney General conviction, 2024

n: Trafigura
d: Convicted in Switzerland in 2024 of failing to prevent bribery in Angola, the second major trader convicted in a Swiss court, and separately settled with Brazilian and US authorities. Physical commodity trading moves value across borders in a form that no financial regulator sees, which is the property this layer records.
cite: Swiss Federal Criminal Court judgment, 2024; US Department of Justice resolution, 2024; Brazilian leniency agreement

n: Michoacan agriculture
d: Extortion of avocado and lime growers, packing houses and hauliers is documented by Mexican federal authorities and by US inspection suspensions after threats to inspectors. The organisations mapped in Tierra Caliente take a fee per hectare and per shipment. Growers and packers are victims of the arrangement, not parties to it, which is why the entry names the sector rather than a company.
cite: US Department of Agriculture APHIS inspection suspensions, 2022 and 2024; Mexican Fiscalia General de la Republica reporting; Michoacan state agricultural association statements
rank: Avocado and lime supply chains (gold, commodities & agribusiness)

n: Amazon gold and timber
d: Illegal gold from the Brazilian, Peruvian and Venezuelan Amazon enters refining chains that also process legitimate metal, and the proceeds settle alongside cocaine proceeds moving on the same rivers. OFAC has designated related networks and Brazilian operations have seized aircraft and dredges at scale. Gold is the preferred store of value on this corridor because it does not decay and carries no serial number.
cite: US Treasury OFAC designations; Brazilian IBAMA and Policia Federal operations, 2021-2024; UNODC and Igarape Institute Amazon reporting

n: Huachicol fiscal — the fuel import chain
d: Mexican authorities arrested serving and former naval officers, customs officials and business figures in 2025 over a scheme importing fuel declared as lubricant additive to evade duty, moving through the ports the navy itself controls. It is the largest documented instance of an armed force's own customs role being used commercially, and the same terminals handle the container traffic on this map's routes.
cite: Mexican Fiscalia General de la Republica and Secretaria de Marina statements, 2025; Mexican federal court filings
rank: Fuel importation and customs (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
